1	"""Item model for the package-sync pipeline (D-02, ADR-020).
2	
3	Item identity is the primary key for the whole subsystem: every package, apt source,
4	signing key, pin, config file, snap, snap channel, flatpak ref, flatpak remote and
5	unreproducible install this phase handles is identified by a stable `item_id` string,
6	not by any manager-specific value. A package name, a flatpak ref, a filename — each is
7	a FIELD of one variant's dataclass, never the primary key itself. This is what lets the
8	shared diff/review/decision-file pipeline in `packages/sync_core.py` operate on one shape
9	(`ItemDiff`) regardless of which manager or item class produced it.
10	
11	This module is the phase's single registry of item shapes: the manager jobs built in
12	plans 02-07 (snap_sync), 02-08 and 02-09 (flatpak_sync, unreproducible-item detection)
13	import `SnapItem`, `FlatpakItem`, `FlatpakRemoteItem` and `UnreproducibleItem` from here
14	and add none of their own. Those three plans are written and run in parallel — a shape
15	defined in three places is a shape that drifts. No plan after wave 4 modifies this
16	module, which is what lets 02-07/02-08/02-09 run in one wave with disjoint file sets.
17	
18	`ItemClass` and `DiffClass` declare their full D-02/D-25 member sets so item types and
19	diff directions were always addable without reopening these enums' shape; this plan
20	(02-05) is where every remaining `DiffClass` member and the four remaining item
21	dataclasses actually arrive.
22	
23	Plan 02-06 adds the four `/etc/apt/*`-adjacent item classes (`AptSourceItem`,
24	`AptKeyItem`, `AptPinItem`, `AptConfigItem`) and is the last plan permitted to modify
25	this module (02-05's own note). Each is identified by its FILENAME, not by any value
26	parsed from its content: RESEARCH's Pitfall 3 documents that a legacy `.list` file and
27	a deb822 `.sources` file can legitimately coexist in `sources.list.d` describing the
28	same repository (e.g. after a partial `apt modernize-sources` run), and identifying by
29	filename is what keeps that pair visible in the review as two distinct items rather
30	than one merged one — the "conflicting values" failure mode apt itself raises when both
31	exist stays a fact the user sees, not something this tool silently resolves for them.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import shlex
37	from dataclasses import dataclass
38	from enum import StrEnum
39	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, ClassVar, Literal
40	
41	if TYPE_CHECKING:
42	    from pcswitcher.executor import Executor
43	
44	__all__ = [
45	    "AptConfigItem",
46	    "AptHoldItem",
47	    "AptKeyItem",
48	    "AptPackageItem",
49	    "AptPinItem",
50	    "AptSourceItem",
51	    "DiffAction",
52	    "DiffClass",
53	    "FlatpakItem",
54	    "FlatpakMaskItem",
55	    "FlatpakRemoteItem",
56	    "HoldPinFact",
57	    "ItemClass",
58	    "ItemDiff",
59	    "SnapItem",
60	    "UnreproducibleItem",
61	    "build_dangling_keyring_detail",
62	    "build_held_or_pinned_detail",
63	    "build_repo_unavailable_detail",
64	    "build_version_mismatch_detail",
65	    "compare_deb_versions",
66	]
67	
68	
69	class ItemClass(StrEnum):
70	    """The full D-02 item-class taxonomy.
71	
72	    `APT_PACKAGE` is captured and diffed by `apt_sync` (plan 02-03/02-05). `SNAP`,
73	    `FLATPAK_REF`, `FLATPAK_REMOTE` and `UNREPRODUCIBLE` have item dataclasses (below)
74	    but no capturing job yet — those arrive in plans 02-07..02-09. `SNAP_CHANNEL`
75	    never becomes a standalone item; see `SnapItem`'s docstring.
76	    """
77	
78	    APT_PACKAGE = "apt_package"
79	    APT_SOURCE = "apt_source"
80	    APT_KEY = "apt_key"
81	    APT_PIN = "apt_pin"
82	    APT_CONFIG = "apt_config"
83	    APT_HOLD = "apt_hold"
84	    SNAP = "snap"
85	    SNAP_CHANNEL = "snap_channel"
86	    SNAP_HOLD = "snap_hold"
87	    FLATPAK_REF = "flatpak_ref"
88	    FLATPAK_REMOTE = "flatpak_remote"
89	    FLATPAK_MASK = "flatpak_mask"
90	    UNREPRODUCIBLE = "unreproducible"
91	
92	
93	class DiffClass(StrEnum):
94	    """The full D-25 conflict taxonomy — every member is producible once this plan's
95	    `diff_items` dispatch (`packages/sync_core.py`) is filled out.
96	    """
97	
98	    MISSING_ON_TARGET = "missing_on_target"
99	    EXTRA_ON_TARGET = "extra_on_target"
100	    VERSION_MISMATCH = "version_mismatch"
101	    HELD_OR_PINNED = "held_or_pinned"
102	    REPO_UNAVAILABLE = "repo_unavailable"
103	    UNREPRODUCIBLE = "unreproducible"
104	
105	
106	class DiffAction(StrEnum):
107	    """The concrete converge verb a diff implies (D-07's direction-dependent "apply").
108	
109	    Values match `packages.review`'s private removal-action set (`{"remove", "delete",
110	    "disable"}`) so a `ReviewGroup` built from these actions gets the right
111	    default-checked/unchecked behavior without that module knowing this enum exists.
112	    """
113	
114	    INSTALL = "install"
115	    REMOVE = "remove"
116	    CHANGE = "change"
117	    REPORT_ONLY = "report_only"
118	
119	
120	@dataclass(frozen=True)
121	class AptPackageItem:
122	    """One manually-installed apt package (D-03), captured from `apt-mark showmanual`
123	    plus one batched `dpkg-query` call for versions.
124	    """
125	
126	    name: str
127	    version: str
128	
129	    @property
130	    def item_id(self) -> str:
131	        """Stable identity string: `apt:package:<name>`."""
132	        return f"apt:package:{self.name}"
133	
134	    def label(self) -> str:
135	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
136	        return f"{self.name} ({self.version})" if self.version else self.name
137	
138	
139	@dataclass(frozen=True)
140	class ItemDiff:
141	    """One item's diff result — the one shape the review and converge loop both consume.
142	
143	    This is D-02's "all classes flow through one pipeline" made real: regardless of
144	    which manager or item class produced it, `PackageSyncJob.apply()` and
145	    `packages.review.review_items()` only ever see `ItemDiff`/`ReviewEntry` shapes.
146	    """
147	
148	    item_class: ItemClass
149	    diff_class: DiffClass
150	    action: DiffAction
151	    item_id: str
152	    label: str
153	    detail: str | None = None
154	
155	
156	async def compare_deb_versions(executor: Executor, left: str, right: str) -> int:
157	    """Compare two Debian package version strings, `sorted`-comparator convention.
158	
159	    Returns negative when `left` < `right`, zero when equal, positive when `left` >
160	    `right`. Not hand-rolled: Debian version ordering has epoch, tilde and revision
161	    tie-breaking rules that are neither lexicographic nor PEP 440 — only dpkg's own
162	    comparator correctly ranks an epoch-bearing version like `2:1.0` above `10.0`
163	    (RESEARCH Don't Hand-Roll). Shells out through `executor` (never assumes a local
164	    `dpkg`, since the target's version may need comparing against its own dpkg) with
165	    `shlex.quote` on both operands (ASVS V5, T-02-01). Short-circuits to equal for
166	    byte-identical strings so the common "nothing changed" case costs no subprocess.
167	    """
168	    if left == right:
169	        return 0
170	
171	    quoted_left = shlex.quote(left)
172	    quoted_right = shlex.quote(right)
173	
174	    lt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} lt {quoted_right}")
175	    if lt_result.success:
176	        return -1
177	
178	    gt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} gt {quoted_right}")
179	    if gt_result.success:
180	        return 1
181	
182	    return 0
183	
184	
185	@dataclass(frozen=True)
186	class HoldPinFact:
187	    """One fact about a package's upgrade being blocked, from one of two distinct
188	    mechanisms (RESEARCH Pitfall 2):
189	
190	    - A HOLD is dpkg *selection state* stored under `/var/lib/dpkg`, read via
191	      `apt-mark showhold`. It blocks ALL upgrades of that package outright.
192	    - A PIN is an apt priority *preference* stored under `/etc/apt/preferences.d`. It
193	      can still allow an upgrade within whatever the pin's priority permits — it is
194	      not an absolute block.
195	
196	    Both surface under the same `DiffClass.HELD_OR_PINNED` review category (D-25), but
197	    they are read from two different sources and mean different things. A diff
198	    implementation that reads only one silently misses every package blocked by the
199	    other mechanism, which is why `mechanism` and `source_ref` stay on this fact
200	    rather than being collapsed into a single boolean.
201	    """
202	
203	    mechanism: Literal["hold", "pin"]
204	    package: str
205	    source_ref: str
206	
207	
208	def build_version_mismatch_detail(source_version: str, target_version: str) -> str:
209	    """Detail string for a `VERSION_MISMATCH` diff: both versions, machine-labelled.
210	
211	    Showing both versions in the review text is what makes D-04's "detected and
212	    reported, never force-downgraded" promise visible to the user — nothing here
213	    proposes a resolution, it names the two facts and leaves the decision alone.
214	    """
215	    return f"source has {source_version}, target has {target_version}"
216	
217	
218	def build_held_or_pinned_detail(fact: HoldPinFact) -> str:
219	    """Detail string for a `HELD_OR_PINNED` diff: names the mechanism and its origin
220	    so a hold and a pin never read as the same fact in the review, even though both
221	    surface under one category (RESEARCH Pitfall 2).
222	    """
223	    verb = "held" if fact.mechanism == "hold" else "pinned"
224	    return f"{verb} ({fact.mechanism}, via {fact.source_ref})"
225	
226	
227	def build_repo_unavailable_detail(name: str) -> str:
228	    """Detail string for a `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` diff: the target's own repositories
229	    offer no installable candidate for this package (`apt-cache policy` showed none).
230	    This must read as its own fact, not silently downgrade to a proposed `INSTALL`.
231	    """
232	    return f"target's repositories offer no candidate for {name}"
233	
234	
235	def build_dangling_keyring_detail(filename: str, missing_ref: str) -> str:
236	    """Detail string when a source file's `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` reference resolves
237	    to no keyring file on the SOURCE itself (a source referencing a key nobody
238	    captured). Flags the source item rather than letting it be proposed for install on
239	    its own (D-12): a repository written without its key is a repository apt refuses on
240	    every subsequent operation, so surfacing the gap here is cheaper than discovering it
241	    as an opaque apt-get failure on the target.
242	    """
243	    return f"{filename} references keyring {missing_ref!r}, which does not exist on the source"
244	
245	
246	@dataclass(frozen=True)
247	class AptSourceItem:
248	    """One apt repository definition file under `/etc/apt/sources.list.d` (D-11).
249	
250	    Identity is the FILENAME (module docstring), not the parsed repository URI: a
251	    legacy `.list` and a deb822 `.sources` file can coexist describing the same repo
252	    (RESEARCH Pitfall 3), and filename identity is what keeps that visible as two
253	    review entries rather than one silently merged one. `fmt` records which shape the
254	    file had so a converged copy preserves it — this tool never normalises one format
255	    into the other (that migration is explicitly deferred, see CONTEXT.md's deferred
256	    ideas). `keyring_refs` holds every `Signed-By:` (deb822) / `signed-by=` (legacy)
257	    path this file names, so the source item's dependency on its key(s) is a captured
258	    fact, not something re-derived by re-parsing the file at convergence time.
259	    """
260	
261	    filename: str
262	    digest: str
263	    fmt: Literal["deb822", "list"]
264	    keyring_refs: tuple[str, ...] = ()
265	
266	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_SOURCE
267	
268	    @property
269	    def item_id(self) -> str:
270	        """Stable identity string: `apt:source:<filename>`."""
271	        return f"apt:source:{self.filename}"
272	
273	    def label(self) -> str:
274	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs, naming the file's format so
275	        a reviewer can tell a `.list` repo from a `.sources` one at a glance.
276	        """
277	        return f"{self.filename} ({self.fmt})"
278	
279	
280	@dataclass(frozen=True)
281	class AptKeyItem:
282	    """One apt signing-key file (D-12), either per-repo (`/etc/apt/keyrings`) or
283	    legacy global-trust (`/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d`).
284	
285	    `scope` keeps the two populations distinct even though both are "a key file":
286	    a per-repo key is referenced by exactly the source item(s) whose `keyring_refs`
287	    name its path, while a global-trust key is referenced by none (RESEARCH: apt-key
288	    deprecated Ubuntu 20.10+, but existing `trusted.gpg.d` entries still work and are
289	    copied verbatim, never migrated). Keys always travel byte-for-byte — this item
290	    never re-fetches or re-derives key content, only compares/transfers the bytes the
291	    source machine already has.
292	    """
293	
294	    filename: str
295	    digest: str
296	    scope: Literal["per-repo", "global-trust"]
297	
298	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_KEY
299	
300	    @property
301	    def item_id(self) -> str:
302	        """Stable identity string: `apt:key:<scope>:<filename>`."""
303	        return f"apt:key:{self.scope}:{self.filename}"
304	
305	    def label(self) -> str:
306	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
307	        return f"{self.filename} ({self.scope} key)"
308	
309	
310	@dataclass(frozen=True)
311	class AptPinItem:
312	    """One apt pin-preference file under `/etc/apt/preferences.d` (D-13).
313	
314	    Diffed by whole-file digest, not by parsed stanza (RESEARCH's alternatives table
315	    recommends whole-file for v1; CONTEXT.md leaves the choice to discretion) —
316	    `pinned_packages` is populated by whichever caller parses the file's content (this
317	    module's diff-time capture, or `AptSyncJob.collect_hold_pin_facts`'s own read) and
318	    stays empty when only the digest was needed to decide there was no diff at all.
319	    """
320	
321	    filename: str
322	    digest: str
323	    pinned_packages: tuple[str, ...] = ()
324	
325	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_PIN
326	
327	    @property
328	    def item_id(self) -> str:
329	        """Stable identity string: `apt:pin:<filename>`."""
330	        return f"apt:pin:{self.filename}"
331	
332	    def label(self) -> str:
333	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
334	        return self.filename
335	
336	
337	@dataclass(frozen=True)
338	class AptConfigItem:
339	    """One apt behavior-configuration file under `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` (D-13).
340	
341	    Synced as an opaque item — whole-file digest only, no parsing of apt's config
342	    grammar — since these files are plain, hand-authored `Acquire::.../APT::...`
343	    stanzas with no sub-item this phase needs to address individually.
344	    """
345	
346	    filename: str
347	    digest: str
348	
349	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_CONFIG
350	
351	    @property
352	    def item_id(self) -> str:
353	        """Stable identity string: `apt:config:<filename>`."""
354	        return f"apt:config:{self.filename}"
355	
356	    def label(self) -> str:
357	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
358	        return self.filename
359	
360	
361	@dataclass(frozen=True)
362	class AptHoldItem:
363	    """One apt package hold (#208): dpkg selection state read via `apt-mark showhold`.
364	
365	    A hold is boolean-membership: a package is either held or it is not, so this item
366	    carries only the package `name` and diffs as a presence difference (source-held &
367	    target-not -> add the hold; target-held & source-not -> remove it). Its identity
368	    (`apt:hold:<name>`) is DISTINCT from the package item's (`apt:package:<name>`) so a
369	    package and its hold are two separate review items — replicating the user's
370	    deliberate "block all upgrades" intent independently of whether the package itself
371	    is being installed this run.
372	    """
373	
374	    name: str
375	
376	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_HOLD
377	
378	    @property
379	    def item_id(self) -> str:
380	        """Stable identity string: `apt:hold:<name>`."""
381	        return f"apt:hold:{self.name}"
382	
383	    def label(self) -> str:
384	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
385	        return f"{self.name} (hold)"
386	
387	
388	@dataclass(frozen=True)
389	class SnapItem:
390	    """One installed snap (D-06): name, tracked channel, and installed revision.
391	
392	    `channel` is a FIELD of the snap item, not a standalone item class:
393	    `ItemClass.SNAP_CHANNEL` is reserved for the diff DETAIL on a channel-only change
394	    (retracking with no revision change) and never becomes a standalone item — a
395	    channel with no snap attached to it has no meaning of its own.
396	
397	    `held` is per-snap refresh-hold state parsed from `snap list` Notes (#208): it is a
398	    FIELD, not part of the snap's identity, and defaults `False` so existing construction
399	    sites and the shared diff never have to name it. `snap_sync` populates it and diffs it
400	    into a separate `snap:hold:<name>` membership item (`ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD`), keeping the
401	    hold a distinct review item from the snap itself.
402	    """
403	
404	    name: str
405	    channel: str
406	    revision: str
407	    held: bool = False
408	
409	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.SNAP
410	
411	    @property
412	    def item_id(self) -> str:
413	        """Stable identity string: `snap:<name>`."""
414	        return f"snap:{self.name}"
415	
416	    def label(self) -> str:
417	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
418	        return f"{self.name} ({self.channel}, revision {self.revision})"
419	
420	
421	@dataclass(frozen=True)
422	class FlatpakItem:
423	    """One installed flatpak application ref (D-06), scoped user or system.
424	
425	    `scope` lives inside the identity string, not just as a field: this project's own
426	    machine has several runtimes installed in both scopes with the same application
427	    id, and folding scope into `item_id` is what makes "same name, different scope"
428	    fall out of the generic diff engine as two distinct items with no special-casing
429	    in `flatpak_sync`.
430	    """
431	
432	    application: str
433	    version: str
434	    origin: str
435	    scope: Literal["user", "system"]
436	
437	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REF
438	
439	    @property
440	    def item_id(self) -> str:
441	        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:ref:<scope>:<application>`."""
442	        return f"flatpak:ref:{self.scope}:{self.application}"
443	
444	    def label(self) -> str:
445	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
446	        return f"{self.application} ({self.version}, {self.origin}, {self.scope})"
447	
448	
449	@dataclass(frozen=True)
450	class FlatpakRemoteItem:
451	    """One configured flatpak remote (D-11/D-14), scoped user or system.
452	
453	    Flatpak tracks remotes per-installation: `flathub` commonly exists in both scopes
454	    with a byte-identical URL, yet the two are separate configuration the target must
455	    provision separately. `scope` inside `item_id` (same reasoning as `FlatpakItem`)
456	    is what keeps those two facts distinct rather than colliding on the shared name.
457	    """
458	
459	    name: str
460	    url: str
461	    scope: Literal["user", "system"]
462	
463	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REMOTE
464	
465	    @property

467	        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:remote:<scope>:<name>`."""
468	        return f"flatpak:remote:{self.scope}:{self.name}"

480	    replicated as a PURE pattern — never filtered to installed refs (D-10) — so a mask
481	    edit reads as remove-old + add-new and a scope split as add + remove, reported as
482	    found rather than normalised. `scope` lives inside `item_id` (same reasoning as
483	    `FlatpakItem`/`FlatpakRemoteItem`) so the same pattern masked in both scopes falls

505	    candidate, or an unowned install under `/usr/local`/`/opt`.

508	    exists but has nothing to install from) versus `unowned-path` (a filesystem path
509	    dpkg does not claim) — and lives inside `item_id` for the same reason `scope`
510	    lives inside the two flatpak identities: the same `identifier` value can appear
511	    under both origins with no relation to each other (e.g. a package name that is
512	    also, coincidentally, a path component), so origin has to be part of identity, not
513	    just a field alongside it.
514	
515	    Unlike the other item types, `label` here is a plain FIELD rather than a `label()`
516	    method: the human-readable description comes from whichever detector found the
517	    item (D-19's unowned-install scan, or the no-candidate check) and is not something
518	    this dataclass can derive from `origin`/`identifier` alone.
519	    """
520	
521	    origin: Literal["apt-no-candidate", "unowned-path"]
522	    identifier: str
523	    label: str
524	
525	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE
526	
527	    @property
528	    def item_id(self) -> str:

"""Item model for the package-sync pipeline (D-02, ADR-020).

Item identity is the primary key for the whole subsystem: every package, apt source,
signing key, pin, config file, snap, snap channel, flatpak ref, flatpak remote and
unreproducible install this phase handles is identified by a stable `item_id` string,
not by any manager-specific value. A package name, a flatpak ref, a filename — each is
a FIELD of one variant's dataclass, never the primary key itself. This is what lets the
shared diff/review/decision-file pipeline in `packages/sync_core.py` operate on one shape
(`ItemDiff`) regardless of which manager or item class produced it.

This module is the phase's single registry of item shapes: the manager jobs built in
plans 02-07 (snap_sync), 02-08 and 02-09 (flatpak_sync, unreproducible-item detection)
import `SnapItem`, `FlatpakItem`, `FlatpakRemoteItem` and `UnreproducibleItem` from here
and add none of their own. Those three plans are written and run in parallel — a shape
defined in three places is a shape that drifts. No plan after wave 4 modifies this
module, which is what lets 02-07/02-08/02-09 run in one wave with disjoint file sets.

`ItemClass` and `DiffClass` declare their full D-02/D-25 member sets so item types and
diff directions were always addable without reopening these enums' shape; this plan
(02-05) is where every remaining `DiffClass` member and the four remaining item
dataclasses actually arrive.

Plan 02-06 adds the four `/etc/apt/*`-adjacent item classes (`AptSourceItem`,
`AptKeyItem`, `AptPinItem`, `AptConfigItem`) and is the last plan permitted to modify
this module (02-05's own note). Each is identified by its FILENAME, not by any value
parsed from its content: RESEARCH's Pitfall 3 documents that a legacy `.list` file and
a deb822 `.sources` file can legitimately coexist in `sources.list.d` describing the
same repository (e.g. after a partial `apt modernize-sources` run), and identifying by
filename is what keeps that pair visible in the review as two distinct items rather
than one merged one — the "conflicting values" failure mode apt itself raises when both
exist stays a fact the user sees, not something this tool silently resolves for them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shlex
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, ClassVar, Literal

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pcswitcher.executor import Executor

__all__ = [
    "AptConfigItem",
    "AptHoldItem",
    "AptKeyItem",
    "AptPackageItem",
    "AptPinItem",
    "AptSourceItem",
    "DiffAction",
    "DiffClass",
    "FlatpakItem",
    "FlatpakMaskItem",
    "FlatpakRemoteItem",
    "HoldPinFact",
    "ItemClass",
    "ItemDiff",
    "SnapItem",
    "UnreproducibleItem",
    "build_dangling_keyring_detail",
    "build_held_or_pinned_detail",
    "build_repo_unavailable_detail",
    "build_version_mismatch_detail",
    "compare_deb_versions",
]


class ItemClass(StrEnum):
    """The full D-02 item-class taxonomy.

    `APT_PACKAGE` is captured and diffed by `apt_sync` (plan 02-03/02-05). `SNAP`,
    `FLATPAK_REF`, `FLATPAK_REMOTE` and `UNREPRODUCIBLE` have item dataclasses (below)
    but no capturing job yet — those arrive in plans 02-07..02-09. `SNAP_CHANNEL`
    never becomes a standalone item; see `SnapItem`'s docstring.
    """

    APT_PACKAGE = "apt_package"
    APT_SOURCE = "apt_source"
    APT_KEY = "apt_key"
    APT_PIN = "apt_pin"
    APT_CONFIG = "apt_config"
    APT_HOLD = "apt_hold"
    SNAP = "snap"
    SNAP_CHANNEL = "snap_channel"
    SNAP_HOLD = "snap_hold"
    FLATPAK_REF = "flatpak_ref"
    FLATPAK_REMOTE = "flatpak_remote"
    FLATPAK_MASK = "flatpak_mask"
    UNREPRODUCIBLE = "unreproducible"


class DiffClass(StrEnum):
    """The full D-25 conflict taxonomy — every member is producible once this plan's
    `diff_items` dispatch (`packages/sync_core.py`) is filled out.
    """

    MISSING_ON_TARGET = "missing_on_target"
    EXTRA_ON_TARGET = "extra_on_target"
    VERSION_MISMATCH = "version_mismatch"
    HELD_OR_PINNED = "held_or_pinned"
    REPO_UNAVAILABLE = "repo_unavailable"
    UNREPRODUCIBLE = "unreproducible"


class DiffAction(StrEnum):
    """The concrete converge verb a diff implies (D-07's direction-dependent "apply").

    Values match `packages.review`'s private removal-action set (`{"remove", "delete",
    "disable"}`) so a `ReviewGroup` built from these actions gets the right
    default-checked/unchecked behavior without that module knowing this enum exists.
    """

    INSTALL = "install"
    REMOVE = "remove"
    CHANGE = "change"
    REPORT_ONLY = "report_only"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptPackageItem:
    """One manually-installed apt package (D-03), captured from `apt-mark showmanual`
    plus one batched `dpkg-query` call for versions.
    """

    name: str
    version: str

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:package:<name>`."""
        return f"apt:package:{self.name}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.name} ({self.version})" if self.version else self.name


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ItemDiff:
    """One item's diff result — the one shape the review and converge loop both consume.

    This is D-02's "all classes flow through one pipeline" made real: regardless of
    which manager or item class produced it, `PackageSyncJob.apply()` and
    `packages.review.review_items()` only ever see `ItemDiff`/`ReviewEntry` shapes.
    """

    item_class: ItemClass
    diff_class: DiffClass
    action: DiffAction
    item_id: str
    label: str
    detail: str | None = None


async def compare_deb_versions(executor: Executor, left: str, right: str) -> int:
    """Compare two Debian package version strings, `sorted`-comparator convention.

    Returns negative when `left` < `right`, zero when equal, positive when `left` >
    `right`. Not hand-rolled: Debian version ordering has epoch, tilde and revision
    tie-breaking rules that are neither lexicographic nor PEP 440 — only dpkg's own
    comparator correctly ranks an epoch-bearing version like `2:1.0` above `10.0`
    (RESEARCH Don't Hand-Roll). Shells out through `executor` (never assumes a local
    `dpkg`, since the target's version may need comparing against its own dpkg) with
    `shlex.quote` on both operands (ASVS V5, T-02-01). Short-circuits to equal for
    byte-identical strings so the common "nothing changed" case costs no subprocess.
    """
    if left == right:
        return 0

    quoted_left = shlex.quote(left)
    quoted_right = shlex.quote(right)

    lt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} lt {quoted_right}")
    if lt_result.success:
        return -1

    gt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} gt {quoted_right}")
    if gt_result.success:
        return 1

    return 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HoldPinFact:
    """One fact about a package's upgrade being blocked, from one of two distinct
    mechanisms (RESEARCH Pitfall 2):

    - A HOLD is dpkg *selection state* stored under `/var/lib/dpkg`, read via
      `apt-mark showhold`. It blocks ALL upgrades of that package outright.
    - A PIN is an apt priority *preference* stored under `/etc/apt/preferences.d`. It
      can still allow an upgrade within whatever the pin's priority permits — it is
      not an absolute block.

    Both surface under the same `DiffClass.HELD_OR_PINNED` review category (D-25), but
    they are read from two different sources and mean different things. A diff
    implementation that reads only one silently misses every package blocked by the
    other mechanism, which is why `mechanism` and `source_ref` stay on this fact
    rather than being collapsed into a single boolean.
    """

    mechanism: Literal["hold", "pin"]
    package: str
    source_ref: str


def build_version_mismatch_detail(source_version: str, target_version: str) -> str:
    """Detail string for a `VERSION_MISMATCH` diff: both versions, machine-labelled.

    Showing both versions in the review text is what makes D-04's "detected and
    reported, never force-downgraded" promise visible to the user — nothing here
    proposes a resolution, it names the two facts and leaves the decision alone.
    """
    return f"source has {source_version}, target has {target_version}"


def build_held_or_pinned_detail(fact: HoldPinFact) -> str:
    """Detail string for a `HELD_OR_PINNED` diff: names the mechanism and its origin
    so a hold and a pin never read as the same fact in the review, even though both
    surface under one category (RESEARCH Pitfall 2).
    """
    verb = "held" if fact.mechanism == "hold" else "pinned"
    return f"{verb} ({fact.mechanism}, via {fact.source_ref})"


def build_repo_unavailable_detail(name: str) -> str:
    """Detail string for a `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` diff: the target's own repositories
    offer no installable candidate for this package (`apt-cache policy` showed none).
    This must read as its own fact, not silently downgrade to a proposed `INSTALL`.
    """
    return f"target's repositories offer no candidate for {name}"


def build_dangling_keyring_detail(filename: str, missing_ref: str) -> str:
    """Detail string when a source file's `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` reference resolves
    to no keyring file on the SOURCE itself (a source referencing a key nobody
    captured). Flags the source item rather than letting it be proposed for install on
    its own (D-12): a repository written without its key is a repository apt refuses on
    every subsequent operation, so surfacing the gap here is cheaper than discovering it
    as an opaque apt-get failure on the target.
    """
    return f"{filename} references keyring {missing_ref!r}, which does not exist on the source"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptSourceItem:
    """One apt repository definition file under `/etc/apt/sources.list.d` (D-11).

    Identity is the FILENAME (module docstring), not the parsed repository URI: a
    legacy `.list` and a deb822 `.sources` file can coexist describing the same repo
    (RESEARCH Pitfall 3), and filename identity is what keeps that visible as two
    review entries rather than one silently merged one. `fmt` records which shape the
    file had so a converged copy preserves it — this tool never normalises one format
    into the other (that migration is explicitly deferred, see CONTEXT.md's deferred
    ideas). `keyring_refs` holds every `Signed-By:` (deb822) / `signed-by=` (legacy)
    path this file names, so the source item's dependency on its key(s) is a captured
    fact, not something re-derived by re-parsing the file at convergence time.
    """

    filename: str
    digest: str
    fmt: Literal["deb822", "list"]
    keyring_refs: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_SOURCE

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:source:<filename>`."""
        return f"apt:source:{self.filename}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs, naming the file's format so
        a reviewer can tell a `.list` repo from a `.sources` one at a glance.
        """
        return f"{self.filename} ({self.fmt})"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptKeyItem:
    """One apt signing-key file (D-12), either per-repo (`/etc/apt/keyrings`) or
    legacy global-trust (`/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d`).

    `scope` keeps the two populations distinct even though both are "a key file":
    a per-repo key is referenced by exactly the source item(s) whose `keyring_refs`
    name its path, while a global-trust key is referenced by none (RESEARCH: apt-key
    deprecated Ubuntu 20.10+, but existing `trusted.gpg.d` entries still work and are
    copied verbatim, never migrated). Keys always travel byte-for-byte — this item
    never re-fetches or re-derives key content, only compares/transfers the bytes the
    source machine already has.
    """

    filename: str
    digest: str
    scope: Literal["per-repo", "global-trust"]

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_KEY

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:key:<scope>:<filename>`."""
        return f"apt:key:{self.scope}:{self.filename}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.filename} ({self.scope} key)"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptPinItem:
    """One apt pin-preference file under `/etc/apt/preferences.d` (D-13).

    Diffed by whole-file digest, not by parsed stanza (RESEARCH's alternatives table
    recommends whole-file for v1; CONTEXT.md leaves the choice to discretion) —
    `pinned_packages` is populated by whichever caller parses the file's content (this
    module's diff-time capture, or `AptSyncJob.collect_hold_pin_facts`'s own read) and
    stays empty when only the digest was needed to decide there was no diff at all.
    """

    filename: str
    digest: str
    pinned_packages: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_PIN

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:pin:<filename>`."""
        return f"apt:pin:{self.filename}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return self.filename


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptConfigItem:
    """One apt behavior-configuration file under `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` (D-13).

    Synced as an opaque item — whole-file digest only, no parsing of apt's config
    grammar — since these files are plain, hand-authored `Acquire::.../APT::...`
    stanzas with no sub-item this phase needs to address individually.
    """

    filename: str
    digest: str

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_CONFIG

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:config:<filename>`."""
        return f"apt:config:{self.filename}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return self.filename


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AptHoldItem:
    """One apt package hold (#208): dpkg selection state read via `apt-mark showhold`.

    A hold is boolean-membership: a package is either held or it is not, so this item
    carries only the package `name` and diffs as a presence difference (source-held &
    target-not -> add the hold; target-held & source-not -> remove it). Its identity
    (`apt:hold:<name>`) is DISTINCT from the package item's (`apt:package:<name>`) so a
    package and its hold are two separate review items — replicating the user's
    deliberate "block all upgrades" intent independently of whether the package itself
    is being installed this run.
    """

    name: str

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.APT_HOLD

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `apt:hold:<name>`."""
        return f"apt:hold:{self.name}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.name} (hold)"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SnapItem:
    """One installed snap (D-06): name, tracked channel, and installed revision.

    `channel` is a FIELD of the snap item, not a standalone item class:
    `ItemClass.SNAP_CHANNEL` is reserved for the diff DETAIL on a channel-only change
    (retracking with no revision change) and never becomes a standalone item — a
    channel with no snap attached to it has no meaning of its own.

    `held` is per-snap refresh-hold state parsed from `snap list` Notes (#208): it is a
    FIELD, not part of the snap's identity, and defaults `False` so existing construction
    sites and the shared diff never have to name it. `snap_sync` populates it and diffs it
    into a separate `snap:hold:<name>` membership item (`ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD`), keeping the
    hold a distinct review item from the snap itself.
    """

    name: str
    channel: str
    revision: str
    held: bool = False

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.SNAP

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `snap:<name>`."""
        return f"snap:{self.name}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.name} ({self.channel}, revision {self.revision})"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlatpakItem:
    """One installed flatpak application ref (D-06), scoped user or system.

    `scope` lives inside the identity string, not just as a field: this project's own
    machine has several runtimes installed in both scopes with the same application
    id, and folding scope into `item_id` is what makes "same name, different scope"
    fall out of the generic diff engine as two distinct items with no special-casing
    in `flatpak_sync`.
    """

    application: str
    version: str
    origin: str
    scope: Literal["user", "system"]

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REF

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:ref:<scope>:<application>`."""
        return f"flatpak:ref:{self.scope}:{self.application}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.application} ({self.version}, {self.origin}, {self.scope})"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlatpakRemoteItem:
    """One configured flatpak remote (D-11/D-14), scoped user or system.

    Flatpak tracks remotes per-installation: `flathub` commonly exists in both scopes
    with a byte-identical URL, yet the two are separate configuration the target must
    provision separately. `scope` inside `item_id` (same reasoning as `FlatpakItem`)
    is what keeps those two facts distinct rather than colliding on the shared name.
    """

    name: str
    url: str
    scope: Literal["user", "system"]

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REMOTE

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:remote:<scope>:<name>`."""
        return f"flatpak:remote:{self.scope}:{self.name}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.name} remote ({self.scope}): {self.url}"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlatpakMaskItem:
    """One flatpak mask pattern (#208, D-10), scoped user or system.

    A mask is a pattern flatpak refuses to install or update (`flatpak mask <pattern>`),
    replicated as a PURE pattern — never filtered to installed refs (D-10) — so a mask
    edit reads as remove-old + add-new and a scope split as add + remove, reported as
    found rather than normalised. `scope` lives inside `item_id` (same reasoning as
    `FlatpakItem`/`FlatpakRemoteItem`) so the same pattern masked in both scopes falls
    out of the generic diff as two distinct items.
    """

    pattern: str
    scope: Literal["user", "system"]

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_MASK

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:mask:<scope>:<pattern>`."""
        return f"flatpak:mask:{self.scope}:{self.pattern}"

    def label(self) -> str:
        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
        return f"{self.pattern} (mask, {self.scope})"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UnreproducibleItem:
    """One item no package manager can reproduce (D-18): an apt package with no repo
    candidate, or an unowned install under `/usr/local`/`/opt`.

    `origin` distinguishes how the item was found — `apt-no-candidate` (a name that
    exists but has nothing to install from) versus `unowned-path` (a filesystem path
    dpkg does not claim) — and lives inside `item_id` for the same reason `scope`
    lives inside the two flatpak identities: the same `identifier` value can appear
    under both origins with no relation to each other (e.g. a package name that is
    also, coincidentally, a path component), so origin has to be part of identity, not
    just a field alongside it.

    Unlike the other item types, `label` here is a plain FIELD rather than a `label()`
    method: the human-readable description comes from whichever detector found the
    item (D-19's unowned-install scan, or the no-candidate check) and is not something
    this dataclass can derive from `origin`/`identifier` alone.
    """

    origin: Literal["apt-no-candidate", "unowned-path"]
    identifier: str
    label: str

    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE

    @property
    def item_id(self) -> str:
        """Stable identity string: `unreproducible:<origin>:<identifier>`."""
        return f"unreproducible:{self.origin}:{self.identifier}"

1	"""Shared package-sync pipeline: `PackageSyncJob`'s plan()/review/apply() split (D-15, D-16, D-24).
2	
3	Every package job (`apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync`) is independent (D-15): its own
4	config, enable flag, failure isolation and progress. D-24 requires each job to present its
5	own batched review before that job's own first mutating command — the batching is per
6	manager, never across managers. The split of `plan()` from `apply()` exists to make that
7	review-before-any-change ordering checkable and testable per job:
8	
9	- `plan()` captures the source manifest, queries the target, diffs, and builds this job's
10	  own `ReviewGroup`s. It issues READ commands only — nothing here may mutate either
11	  machine, because a job plans and reviews before it converges. Before capturing anything,
12	  it loads both machines' machine-local decision files (D-08, D-09, `packages/state.py`) and
13	  filters an inert item out of the side that holds it, so an item recorded "skip always"
14	  never becomes an `ItemDiff` in the first place — D-08's "inert on M in both roles" made
15	  real at the diff-input boundary rather than as a later filter on the review.
16	- `accept_review()` stores this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned, so
17	  `apply()` and the apt guards read a consistent pair.
18	- `apply()` converges the `APPLY`-decided diffs, one item at a time, catching and
19	  collecting per-item failures (D-27) so one bad item never stops the rest. It also
20	  persists a permanent decision (D-08a) for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item, on
21	  whichever machine holds it.
22	- `execute()` — the `SyncJob` entry point the orchestrator's sequential loop calls — is
23	  self-contained: it plans, reviews through the injected `JobContext.reviewer`, accepts the
24	  outcome, then applies. A `plan()` failure propagates naturally out of `execute()` and
25	  lands in this job's own `JobResult` through the orchestrator's per-job exception handling.

77	    chain can distinguish "this job's items failed" (continue running the remaining
78	    package jobs — their diffs were already approved in the same review) from "this job
79	    crashed" (abort the whole run, today's existing behavior for every other exception).
80	    """

83	        self.manager = manager
84	        self.failures = tuple(failures)
85	        names = ", ".join(diff.label for diff, _stderr in failures)
86	        super().__init__(f"{len(failures)} {manager} item(s) failed to converge: {names}")

94	    per D-07/D-24) so `execute()` passes them straight to the reviewer without re-deriving

103	# The concrete converge verb for one (item_class, action) pair (D-07, D-24): "apply" is
104	# never shown to the user, because it is the destructive branch as often as the
105	# additive one. An apt package REMOVE reads as "remove"; a future apt source REMOVE
106	# reads as "delete repository"; a future snap channel CHANGE reads as "retrack". Data,
107	# not per-job string formatting, is what makes "the review names the concrete action"
108	# checkable rather than left to each job's own wording. Entries beyond APT_PACKAGE are
109	# illustrative for item classes this plan defines but does not yet diff (SNAP_CHANNEL,
110	# APT_SOURCE) — `_build_review_groups` falls back to the bare `DiffAction` value for any
111	# (item_class, action) pair not listed here, so a missing vocabulary entry degrades to a
112	# plain verb instead of silently dropping the group (the backstop this plan requires:
113	# every diff class the engine produces gets SOME review presentation).
114	_ACTION_VOCABULARY: dict[tuple[ItemClass, DiffAction], str] = {
115	    (ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE, DiffAction.INSTALL): "install",
116	    (ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE, DiffAction.CHANGE): "change",
117	    (ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE, DiffAction.REMOVE): "remove",
118	    (ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE, DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY): "report",
119	    (ItemClass.APT_SOURCE, DiffAction.REMOVE): "delete repository",
120	    (ItemClass.SNAP_CHANNEL, DiffAction.CHANGE): "retrack",
121	    # Block-state membership items (#208): the add direction reads "hold"/"mask" and the
122	    # remove direction "unhold"/"unmask", never "install"/"remove". `_build_review_groups`
123	    # keys the group title AND every entry's action_label off this table by the group's own
124	    # item class, so a hold/mask item never displays under an "Install/Remove packages"
125	    # group even when it shares a `DiffAction` with a package.
126	    (ItemClass.APT_HOLD, DiffAction.INSTALL): "hold",
127	    (ItemClass.APT_HOLD, DiffAction.REMOVE): "unhold",
128	    (ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD, DiffAction.INSTALL): "hold",
129	    (ItemClass.SNAP_HOLD, DiffAction.REMOVE): "unhold",
130	    (ItemClass.FLATPAK_MASK, DiffAction.INSTALL): "mask",
131	    (ItemClass.FLATPAK_MASK, DiffAction.REMOVE): "unmask",
132	}

134	# Fixed emission order for review groups: install before change before remove keeps
135	# the most common/least-destructive action first; report_only trails since it needs a
136	# decision but implies no direct converge verb.
137	_ACTION_ORDER: tuple[DiffAction, ...] = (
138	    DiffAction.INSTALL,
139	    DiffAction.CHANGE,
140	    DiffAction.REMOVE,
141	    DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
142	)

146	    """Shared plan()/apply() pipeline every package-manager job subclasses.
147	
148	    Deliberately carries NO `name` ClassVar: `Orchestrator._resolve_sync_job_class` scans
149	    a job module's attributes for a `SyncJob` subclass whose `name` matches the module
150	    name (`getattr(attr, "name", None) == job_name`), so an abstract base without `name`

152	    """

154	    manager_id: ClassVar[str]
155	
156	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
157	        super().__init__(context)
158	        self._accepted_plan: PackagePlan | None = None
159	        self._accepted_outcome: ReviewOutcome | None = None

161	    # -- Abstract hooks subclasses implement -------------------------------------------
162	
163	    @abstractmethod
164	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[AptPackageItem]:
165	        """Read this manager's manifest from the source. Read-only."""
166	        ...
167	
168	    @abstractmethod
169	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[AptPackageItem]:
170	        """Read this manager's current state from the target. Read-only."""
171	        ...
172	
173	    @abstractmethod
174	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:

176	
177	        May raise `ConvergeItemFailed` to refuse the item without even attempting the
178	        mutating command (e.g. a transaction-safety guard); otherwise returns the
179	        `CommandResult` of the converge command, whose `.success` decides pass/fail.

185	    async def collect_hold_pin_facts(self) -> Sequence[HoldPinFact]:
186	        """Hold/pin facts (D-25, RESEARCH Pitfall 2) this manager's diff should treat
187	        as `HELD_OR_PINNED` rather than proposing a normal install/remove/change.
188	
189	        Default: none. Only apt has a hold-vs-pin concept (`apt-mark showhold` and
190	        `preferences.d` are two distinct mechanisms); `snap_sync`/`flatpak_sync` need
191	        not override this.

193	        As of #208 this hook carries PIN facts only (the target-only `REPORT_ONLY` echo
194	        on the package item). Apt HOLDS travel as their own `apt:hold:` membership items,
195	        fed by `collect_hold_sets` — not through this hook — so a held package is never

200	    async def collect_hold_sets(self) -> tuple[frozenset[str], frozenset[str]]:
201	        """Source and target package-hold NAME sets feeding the `apt:hold:` membership
202	        diff (#208, D5). Returned as `(source_hold_names, target_hold_names)`.
203	
204	        Default: two empty sets. Only apt overrides this (`apt-mark showhold` on both
205	        machines). The two sets drive `_diff_apt_packages`: a name held on the source but
206	        not the target becomes an `AptHoldItem` INSTALL (hold), the reverse a REMOVE
207	        (unhold), and the target set additionally SUPPRESSES a held package's own
208	        install/upgrade action (a held package is never proposed for install/version
209	        change) without emitting any package-level hold report.
210	        """

213	    async def collect_unavailable_item_ids(self, missing_item_ids: frozenset[str]) -> frozenset[str]:
214	        """Of `missing_item_ids` (items missing on the target), which have no
215	        installable candidate — `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` rather than `MISSING_ON_TARGET`.
216	
217	        Default: none. Only managers whose ecosystem can report "no candidate" (apt
218	        via `apt-cache policy`) need override this.
219	        """

222	    # -- Shared diff -----------------------------------------------------------------
223	
224	    def diff_items(
225	        self,
226	        source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
227	        target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
228	        *,
229	        hold_pin_facts: Sequence[HoldPinFact] = (),
230	        unavailable_item_ids: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
231	        source_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
232	        target_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
233	    ) -> tuple[ItemDiff, ...]:
234	        """Diff source against target into every D-25 `ItemDiff` class.
235	
236	        Structured as a per-item-class dispatch (`_diff_apt_packages` today) so a
237	        later plan adds new item classes by adding more private helpers here rather
238	        than reshaping this method. `hold_pin_facts`, `unavailable_item_ids` and the two
239	        hold-name sets come from the hooks above
240	        (`collect_hold_pin_facts`/`collect_unavailable_item_ids`/`collect_hold_sets`) so
241	        this method stays manager-agnostic — it never shells out itself.
242	        """
243	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
244	        diffs.extend(
245	            self._diff_apt_packages(
246	                source_items,
247	                target_items,
248	                hold_pin_facts,
249	                unavailable_item_ids,
250	                source_hold_names,
251	                target_hold_names,
252	            )
253	        )
254	        return tuple(diffs)

256	    @staticmethod
257	    def _diff_apt_packages(
258	        source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
259	        target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
260	        hold_pin_facts: Sequence[HoldPinFact],
261	        unavailable_item_ids: frozenset[str],
262	        source_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
263	        target_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
264	    ) -> list[ItemDiff]:
265	        """One diff per item id present on either side, source-then-target order,
266	        followed by the `apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D5/D8 — holds emitted AFTER
267	        package diffs so install lands before its hold once the diffs converge).
268	
269	        Precedence per package id: a PINNED package (present on the target and named by a
270	        pin fact) yields `HELD_OR_PINNED`/`REPORT_ONLY` — the pin echo D-25 requires,
271	        informational only. A HELD package (target hold set) has its install/upgrade
272	        action SUPPRESSED (a held package is never proposed for install/version change)
273	        but produces NO package-level report — the hold travels as its own `apt:hold:`
274	        item, so a held package is never double-reported. Otherwise: missing-on-target ->
275	        `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` if apt reports no candidate, else `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`INSTALL`;
276	        extra-on-target -> `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE`; present on both with differing
277	        versions -> `VERSION_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY` (D-04: reported, never
278	        force-downgraded); present on both with equal versions -> no diff at all.
279	
280	        Hold membership (D2): source-held & target-not -> `AptHoldItem` INSTALL (hold);
281	        target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or neither -> no diff.
282	        """
283	        source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
284	        target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
285	
286	        # PINS only (#208, D5): holds no longer key this guard — they travel as their own
287	        # `apt:hold:` items below, so this branch keys purely on the pin mechanism.
288	        pinned: dict[str, HoldPinFact] = {}
289	        for fact in hold_pin_facts:
290	            if fact.mechanism == "pin":
291	                pinned.setdefault(fact.package, fact)
292	
293	        seen: dict[str, None] = {}
294	        for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
295	            seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
296	
297	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
298	        for item_id in seen:
299	            source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
300	            target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
301	
302	            if target_item is not None and target_item.name in pinned:
303	                diffs.append(
304	                    ItemDiff(
305	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
306	                        diff_class=DiffClass.HELD_OR_PINNED,
307	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
308	                        item_id=item_id,
309	                        label=target_item.label(),
310	                        detail=build_held_or_pinned_detail(pinned[target_item.name]),
311	                    )
312	                )
313	            elif target_item is not None and target_item.name in target_hold_names:
314	                # Held on the target: suppress its install/version action entirely (a held
315	                # package must never be proposed for install/upgrade). No package-level
316	                # report — the `apt:hold:` item below carries the hold fact.
317	                continue
318	            elif source_item is not None and target_item is None:
319	                if item_id in unavailable_item_ids:
320	                    diffs.append(
321	                        ItemDiff(
322	                            item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
323	                            diff_class=DiffClass.REPO_UNAVAILABLE,
324	                            action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
325	                            item_id=item_id,
326	                            label=source_item.label(),
327	                            detail=build_repo_unavailable_detail(source_item.name),
328	                        )
329	                    )
330	                else:
331	                    diffs.append(
332	                        ItemDiff(
333	                            item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
334	                            diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET,
335	                            action=DiffAction.INSTALL,
336	                            item_id=item_id,
337	                            label=source_item.label(),
338	                            detail=None,
339	                        )
340	                    )
341	            elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
342	                diffs.append(
343	                    ItemDiff(
344	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
345	                        diff_class=DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
346	                        action=DiffAction.REMOVE,
347	                        item_id=item_id,
348	                        label=target_item.label(),
349	                        detail=None,
350	                    )
351	                )
352	            elif source_item is not None and target_item is not None and source_item.version != target_item.version:
353	                diffs.append(
354	                    ItemDiff(
355	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
356	                        diff_class=DiffClass.VERSION_MISMATCH,
357	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
358	                        item_id=item_id,
359	                        label=target_item.label(),
360	                        detail=build_version_mismatch_detail(source_item.version, target_item.version),
361	                    )
362	                )
363	            # else: present on both, equal versions, not held/pinned -> no diff.
364	
365	        # Hold membership diffs (#208, D2/D8): emitted AFTER every package diff so a
366	        # package install lands before its hold when both are approved.
367	        diffs.extend(PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names, target_hold_names))
368	        return diffs
369	
370	    @staticmethod
371	    def _diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names: frozenset[str], target_hold_names: frozenset[str]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
372	        """`apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D2): source-held & target-not -> INSTALL
373	        (hold); target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or on neither
374	        -> no diff. `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
375	        """
376	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
377	        for name in sorted(source_hold_names | target_hold_names):
378	            in_source = name in source_hold_names
379	            in_target = name in target_hold_names
380	            if in_source == in_target:
381	                continue
382	            hold_item = AptHoldItem(name=name)
383	            diffs.append(
384	                ItemDiff(
385	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_HOLD,
386	                    diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
387	                    action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,
388	                    item_id=hold_item.item_id,
389	                    label=hold_item.label(),
390	                    detail=None,
391	                )
392	            )
393	        return diffs
394	
395	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:
396	        """One `ReviewGroup` per `(action, item_class)` present in `diffs`, keyed on
397	        `(manager, action)` for the reviewer's removal-direction test (D-24) so removals
398	        never share a group with installs. The title's verb and every entry's
399	        `action_label` come from `_ACTION_VOCABULARY`, keyed by the group's own item
400	        class — so a block-state membership item (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`,
401	        `flatpak:mask:`) whose add direction shares the `INSTALL` action with a package
402	        still reads "Hold/Mask ..." rather than displaying under "Install packages"
403	        (#208). Grouping by item class as well as action is what keeps that verb correct
404	        when one action mixes item classes (e.g. apt package INSTALL alongside apt hold
405	        INSTALL); the group's `action` value stays the raw `DiffAction` so add-direction
406	        stays default-checked and remove-direction lands in its own unticked group.
407	
408	        Emission order: `_ACTION_ORDER` (install, change, remove, report) outer, and
409	        within one action the item classes in first-seen order — which, because
410	        `_diff_apt_packages` emits package diffs before hold diffs, keeps a package group
411	        ahead of its hold group.
412	        """
413	        by_key: dict[tuple[DiffAction, ItemClass], list[ItemDiff]] = {}
414	        class_order: dict[DiffAction, list[ItemClass]] = {}
415	        for diff in diffs:
416	            key = (diff.action, diff.item_class)
417	            if key not in by_key:
418	                by_key[key] = []
419	                class_order.setdefault(diff.action, []).append(diff.item_class)
420	            by_key[key].append(diff)
421	
422	        groups: list[ReviewGroup] = []
423	        for action in _ACTION_ORDER:
424	            for item_class in class_order.get(action, []):
425	                entries = by_key[(action, item_class)]
426	                # REPORT_ONLY has no more-specific per-item-class meaning for any current
427	                # manager (IN-01): fall back to "report" rather than the raw enum value
428	                # ("report_only"), which read awkwardly in review text like "Report_only
429	                # flatpak packages". Every other action still falls back to its own
430	                # `action.value`, unchanged.
431	                default_verb = "report" if action == DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else action.value
432	                verb = _ACTION_VOCABULARY.get((item_class, action), default_verb)
433	                groups.append(
434	                    ReviewGroup(
435	                        manager=self.manager_id,
436	                        action=action.value,
437	                        title=f"{verb.capitalize()} {self.manager_id} packages",
438	                        entries=tuple(
439	                            ReviewEntry(item_id=diff.item_id, label=diff.label, action_label=verb, detail=diff.detail)
440	                            for diff in entries
441	                        ),
442	                    )
443	                )
444	        return tuple(groups)
445	
446	    # -- plan() / accept_review() / apply() / execute() -------------------------------
447	
448	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
449	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups. Read-only.
450	
451	        Nothing here may mutate either machine: a job plans and reviews before it
452	        converges, so `plan()` runs before the user has approved anything. Both
453	        machines' decision files are loaded first (a read, like everything else here)
454	        and each side's captured/queried items are filtered through its OWN file before
455	        diffing (D-08): an item recorded on the source is dropped from the source
456	        manifest so it is never pushed to a peer again; an item recorded on the target
457	        is dropped from the target query so it is never proposed for
458	        install/remove/change again — either way it produces no `ItemDiff` and never
459	        reaches the review.
460	        """
461	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
462	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
463	
464	        source_items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
465	        target_items = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
466	        hold_pin_facts = await self.collect_hold_pin_facts()
467	        source_hold_names, target_hold_names = await self.collect_hold_sets()
468	        missing_item_ids = frozenset(item.item_id for item in source_items) - frozenset(
469	            item.item_id for item in target_items
470	        )
471	        unavailable_item_ids = await self.collect_unavailable_item_ids(missing_item_ids)
472	        diffs = self.diff_items(
473	            source_items,
474	            target_items,
475	            hold_pin_facts=hold_pin_facts,
476	            unavailable_item_ids=unavailable_item_ids,
477	            source_hold_names=source_hold_names,
478	            target_hold_names=target_hold_names,
479	        )
480	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
481	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
482	
483	    def accept_review(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
484	        """Store this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned."""
485	        self._accepted_plan = plan
486	        self._accepted_outcome = outcome
487	
488	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
489	        """Hook: work that must run AFTER this job's review returns but BEFORE any
490	        mutation on the target (`apply()`).
491	
492	        No-op on the base — the three managers that produce no unreproducible items (apt,
493	        snap, flatpak) need nothing between review and converge. Only `manual_installs_sync`
494	        overrides it (D-23): it pushes the freshly reconciled install-snippet registry to
495	        the target here, so a snippet the user authored during THIS run's review is on the
496	        target before `apply()` replays it. Keeping the hook on the base leaves `execute()`
497	        the single source of the plan/review/apply order rather than each manager
498	        re-deriving it.
499	        """
500	        return
501	
502	    async def apply(self) -> None:
503	        """Converge every APPLY-decided diff from the accepted plan, one item at a time.
504	
505	        Per-item detail at `LogLevel.FULL`, one `LogLevel.INFO` summary line per job
506	        (ADR-010). A per-item failure (`ConvergeItemFailed`, or a converge command that
507	        exits non-zero) is caught, logged with its stderr as structured context, and
508	        collected — the loop always completes (D-27) — then `PackageItemFailures` is
509	        raised once, after the loop, if anything failed OR anything is left unresolved
510	        (D-21) — even when `total` is zero, since an interactive run whose ONLY diffs
511	        were unreproducible items never has any INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE work to do, and
512	        must still fail if one of them ended up unresolved.
513	
514	        Dry-run (ADR-014): each intended action is logged at FULL with a `[dry-run] `
515	        prefix and no converge command is ever issued.
516	
517	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are excluded here regardless of decision: they imply no
518	        converge verb (D-25's held/pinned, version-mismatch, repo-unavailable,
519	        unreproducible classes are informational), so `converge()` is never called
520	        for one even if something recorded `APPLY` against it.
521	
522	        Before converging anything, `_record_permanent_skips` persists a `DecisionEntry`
523	        for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item (D-08). The `_finalize_unreproducible` hook
524	        then persists this run's authored snippets and unreproducible-item skip-always
525	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23); it is a no-op on the base and only
526	        `manual_installs_sync` implements it (D-18), but the call site stays here so both
527	        run before any converge, independent of whether this run applies anything else
528	        (a run with zero installs but one newly-authored snippet still records it). The
529	        `_unresolved_as_failures` hook (also no-op on the base, overridden only by
530	        `manual_installs_sync`) supplies the genuinely-undecided items that fail an
531	        interactive run — which is why `total == 0` can still raise `PackageItemFailures`.
532	        """
533	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
534	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
535	        plan = self._accepted_plan
536	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
537	        decisions = outcome.decisions
538	
539	        await self._record_permanent_skips(plan, decisions)
540	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(plan, outcome)
541	
542	        apply_diffs = [
543	            diff
544	            for diff in plan.diffs
545	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY and diff.action != DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
546	        ]
547	        prefix = "[dry-run] " if self.context.dry_run else ""
548	        total = len(apply_diffs)
549	
550	        failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]] = []
551	        if total == 0:
552	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}No {self.manager_id} changes to apply")
553	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
554	        else:
555	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}Applying {total} {self.manager_id} change(s)")
556	
557	            for index, diff in enumerate(apply_diffs):
558	                if self.context.dry_run:
559	                    self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{prefix}Would {diff.action.value} {diff.label}")
560	                else:
561	                    await self._converge_one(diff, failures)
562	                self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=int((index + 1) / total * 100)))
563	
564	            succeeded = total - len(failures)
565	            self._log(
566	                Host.TARGET,
567	                LogLevel.INFO,
568	                f"{prefix}{succeeded}/{total} {self.manager_id} change(s) applied",
569	            )
570	
571	        all_failures = [*failures, *self._unresolved_as_failures(plan, outcome)]
572	        if all_failures:
573	            summary = "; ".join(f"{diff.label}: {stderr.strip()}" for diff, stderr in all_failures)
574	            self._log(
575	                Host.TARGET,
576	                LogLevel.INFO,
577	                f"{len(all_failures)} {self.manager_id} item(s) failed: {summary}",
578	            )
579	            raise PackageItemFailures(self.manager_id, all_failures)
580	
581	    def _unresolved_as_failures(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]:
582	        """Hook: this job's genuinely-undecided items that fail an interactive run (D-27).
583	
584	        No-op on the base — it returns an empty list, so the three managers that produce
585	        no unreproducible items (apt, snap, flatpak) never fail on this basis. Only
586	        `manual_installs_sync` overrides it (D-18/D-21): an unreproducible item left with
587	        neither a snippet nor a recorded decision after an interactive review fails the
588	        job. The D-27 converge-failure contract in `apply()` is unchanged — converge
589	        failures fail the job regardless of what this hook returns.
590	        """
591	        return []
592	
593	    async def _finalize_unreproducible(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
594	        """Hook: persist this job's unreproducible-item snippet authoring and skip-always
595	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23).
596	
597	        No-op on the base — only `manual_installs_sync` produces unreproducible items
598	        (D-18), and it overrides this hook with the real persistence; the three managers
599	        that never do inherit this no-op so the base `apply()` stays generic.
600	        """
601	        return
602	
603	    async def _record_permanent_skips(self, plan: PackagePlan, decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> None:
604	        """Persist a `DecisionEntry` for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided, actionable diff.
605	
606	        D-08a decides WHICH machine's file gets the entry by which machine HOLDS the
607	        item: `INSTALL`/`CHANGE` diffs are source-held (the source has the item, or the
608	        version it should converge to), so they record on `self.source`; `REMOVE` diffs
609	        are target-held (only the target has the item), so they record on `self.target`
610	        — through the remote executor, never a local write (ADR-002).
611	
612	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are skipped: they carry no converge verb (version-mismatch,
613	        held/pinned, repo-unavailable, unreproducible are informational only), so there
614	        is no "holder" for D-08a to record against.
615	
616	        Two guards, both required before anything is ever written: never for a
617	        non-interactive outcome (D-26 — nothing is recorded permanently when nothing
618	        was actually decided by a human), and never during a dry run (ADR-014 — a
619	        rehearsal must leave no trace).
620	        """
621	        if self.context.dry_run or not self._accepted_outcome_was_interactive():
622	            return
623	
624	        recorded_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
625	        for diff in plan.diffs:
626	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS:
627	                continue
628	            if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
629	                continue
630	
631	            executor = self.source if diff.action in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE) else self.target
632	            await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, executor).record(
633	                DecisionEntry(
634	                    item_id=diff.item_id,
635	                    item_class=diff.item_class,
636	                    label=diff.label,
637	                    reason=None,
638	                    recorded_at=recorded_at,
639	                )
640	            )
641	
642	    def _accepted_outcome_was_interactive(self) -> bool:
643	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
644	        return self._accepted_outcome.was_interactive
645	
646	    async def _converge_one(self, diff: ItemDiff, failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]) -> None:
647	        try:
648	            result = await self.converge(diff)
649	        except ConvergeItemFailed as exc:
650	            failures.append((diff, str(exc)))
651	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.ERROR, f"{diff.label} failed: {exc}", stderr=str(exc))
652	            return
653	
654	        if result.success:
655	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{diff.action.value} {diff.label}")
656	        else:
657	            failures.append((diff, result.stderr))
658	            self._log(
659	                Host.TARGET,
660	                LogLevel.ERROR,
661	                f"{diff.label} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}",
662	                stderr=result.stderr,
663	            )
664	
665	    async def execute(self) -> None:
666	        """The `SyncJob` entry point the orchestrator's sequential job loop calls.
667	
668	        Self-contained (D-24): plan this job's diffs, review its own groups through the
669	        injected `JobContext.reviewer`, accept the outcome, run the `after_review()` hook
670	        (the seam where `manual_installs_sync` pushes its snippet registry, D-23), then
671	        apply. No component outside the job owns its review, and no fallback applies diffs
672	        that never came back from one — a missing reviewer fails loudly here rather than
673	        silently skipping the review and converging unreviewed diffs (T-02-38).
674	
675	        A `plan()` failure propagates unchanged, so the orchestrator's per-job exception
676	        handling attributes it to this job's own `JobResult`.
677	        """
678	        assert self.context.reviewer is not None, (
679	            f"{self.manager_id} sync has no reviewer; the orchestrator must inject one "
680	            "through JobContext.reviewer before execute()."
681	        )
682	        plan = await self.plan()
683	        outcome = await self.context.reviewer.review(plan.groups)
684	        self.accept_review(plan, outcome)
685	        await self.after_review()
686	        await self.apply()
