"""Per-action confirmation gate behind `--confirm-each-command`.

A package sync run converges dozens of small mutating commands — `apt-get install`,
`snap remove`, `sudo install` into `/etc/apt`, an SFTP push of the snippet registry — each
of which was approved only in aggregate, as a ticked line in a batched review. This gate
inserts one prompt before every single one of them, showing the EXACT operation about to
happen: the literal shell command as it will be passed to the shell, or the local path and
remote destination of a file transfer. Nothing is paraphrased or reconstructed for display,
because a display string that differs from what runs is worse than no display at all.

Distinct from `pcswitcher.confirmer.Confirmer`, which gates ONE coarse decision per run
(first-sync overwrite, out-of-order topology) and falls back to an `--allow-*` flag when
nobody is there to answer. This gate has no such fallback and never auto-proceeds: it is
opt-in per run and refused outright without a TTY (`cli.sync`), because a gate that
auto-proceeds when unanswerable is precisely the failure it exists to prevent.

Two outcomes only, with no default (the user must type one): proceed, or abort the whole
sync. There is deliberately no "skip this command" — a single reviewed item can span
several commands (apt source stage-then-promote, snap install-then-switch-channel), so
skipping one of them leaves that item half-applied, which is a worse state than either
finishing it or stopping.

Generic on purpose, and invoked from exactly one place: `pcswitcher.executor`. Any caller
— job, orchestrator, helper — gates a write by passing `mutates="..."` to the executor
method it already uses, so there is no second API to remember and no per-job wiring. The
executor supplies `job` (from its `active_job` context variable) and `host` (from which
executor it is). Today only the package sync jobs pass `mutates`; `folder_sync` is #209.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from rich.console import Console
from rich.panel import Panel
from rich.prompt import Prompt
from rich.text import Text

from pcswitcher.confirmer import PausableUI
from pcswitcher.models import Host, SyncAbortedByUser

__all__ = ["StepGate", "TerminalUIStepGate"]

_PROCEED = "p"
_ABORT = "a"


@runtime_checkable
class StepGate(Protocol):
    """A per-action confirmation gate: show one pending modification, block, decide."""

    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
        """Show a pending modification and block until the user decides.

        Args:
            job: Name of the job about to modify something (panel heading, log context).
            host: Which machine the modification lands on.
            description: Short human phrase for what this achieves ("install firefox").
            command: The operation VERBATIM — the shell command as it will be executed, or
                a `send_file <local> -> <remote>` rendering for a transfer.

        Returns:
            None when the user chose to proceed.

        Raises:
            SyncAbortedByUser: The user aborted, or the prompt could not be answered
                (EOF / Ctrl-C). Never swallowed into a silent "proceed".
        """
        ...


class TerminalUIStepGate:
    """`StepGate` backed by the Rich console and the live `TerminalUI`.

    Pauses the live display around the blocking prompt for the same reason
    `TerminalUIConfirmer` does — a Rich `Live` and a `Prompt.ask` cannot share the
    terminal — and resumes it in a `finally` so the display is handed back even when the
    prompt raises.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        console: Console,
        ui: PausableUI,
        *,
        logger: logging.Logger | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._console = console
        self._ui = ui
        self._logger = logger if logger is not None else logging.getLogger("pcswitcher.step_gate")

    async def confirm_action(self, *, job: str, host: Host, description: str, command: str) -> None:
        extra = {"job": job, "host": host.value}

        # Body is assembled as a `Text`, never a markup string: `command` is arbitrary
        # content (package names, file paths, snippet bodies) and a stray `[` in it would
        # otherwise be parsed as Rich markup and raise mid-prompt.
        body = Text()
        body.append(f"{job} → {host.value}\n", style="bold")
        body.append(f"{description}\n\n", style="dim")
        body.append(command, style="bold")

        self._ui.pause()
        try:
            self._console.print()
            self._console.print(Panel(body, title="Confirm modification", border_style="yellow"))
            self._console.print()
            # No `default=`: the user must type a choice. An accidental Enter re-prompts
            # rather than picking either outcome for them.
            response = Prompt.ask(
                f"[bold]Run this?[/bold] [{_PROCEED}] proceed  [{_ABORT}] abort sync",
                choices=[_PROCEED, _ABORT],
                show_choices=False,
            )
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) as exc:
            # Unanswerable is not approval: the same rule the review applies to Ctrl-C.
            self._logger.warning("Confirmation prompt interrupted; aborting sync", extra=extra)
            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: confirmation prompt interrupted before {description}") from exc
        finally:
            self._ui.resume()

        if response == _ABORT:
            self._logger.warning("Aborted by user at: %s", description, extra=extra)
            raise SyncAbortedByUser(f"{job}: aborted by user before {description} on {host.value}")
        self._logger.debug("Confirmed: %s", description, extra=extra)

    async def _execute_jobs(self, jobs: list[Job]) -> list[JobResult]:
        """Execute sync jobs sequentially with background disk monitoring.

        Each package job reviews its own diffs inside its own ``execute()`` (D-24): it
        plans, prompts through the injected ``JobContext.reviewer``, then converges. The
        review's blocking prompt runs inside the job TaskGroup alongside the disk-space
        monitors — ``review_items`` pauses the Live display before prompting and resumes
        it in a ``finally``, the same mechanism ``TerminalUIConfirmer`` already uses from
        ``FolderSyncJob.execute()`` — so no coordination outside the TaskGroup is needed.

        Args:
            jobs: List of validated jobs to execute

        Returns:
            List of JobResult for each executed job
        """
        results: list[JobResult] = []

        try:
            await self._run_jobs_in_task_group(jobs, results)
        except BaseExceptionGroup as eg:
            # A job failing in the TaskGroup body raises an ExceptionGroup whose
            # own message ("unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (N sub-exceptions)")
            # is useless. Re-raise the underlying cause so run()'s handlers and
            # the CLI report the real reason — and so a job-raised
            # SyncAbortedByUser/SyncLockedError still reaches its WARNING handler.
            raise _unwrap_taskgroup_error(eg) from None

        return results

    async def _run_jobs_in_task_group(self, jobs: list[Job], results: list[JobResult]) -> None:
        """Run the disk-space monitors and sync jobs inside a single TaskGroup.

        Extracted from ``_execute_jobs`` so the caller can unwrap the
        ExceptionGroup this raises when a job fails (see ``_unwrap_taskgroup_error``).
        """
        assert self._ui is not None

        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            self._task_group = tg

            # Start background disk space monitors for root filesystem
            monitor_config = {
                "preflight_minimum": self._config.disk.preflight_minimum,
                "runtime_minimum": self._config.disk.runtime_minimum,
                "warning_threshold": self._config.disk.warning_threshold,
                "check_interval": self._config.disk.check_interval,
            }
            monitor_context = self._create_job_context(monitor_config)
            source_monitor = DiskSpaceMonitorJob(monitor_context, host=Host.SOURCE, mount_point="/")
            target_monitor = DiskSpaceMonitorJob(monitor_context, host=Host.TARGET, mount_point="/")

            # Start monitors and save tasks for later cancellation
            source_monitor_task = tg.create_task(source_monitor.execute())
            target_monitor_task = tg.create_task(target_monitor.execute())

            try:
                # Execute sync jobs sequentially
                for job_index, job in enumerate(jobs):
                    # Jobs are sub-steps of SyncStep.RUN_JOBS, sub-labelled 10a, 10b, …
                    # (letters suffice for any realistic job count; fall back to a
                    # numeric suffix past 'z'), labelled with the job name so the TUI
                    # shows what is running.
                    substep = chr(ord("a") + job_index) if job_index < 26 else str(job_index + 1)
                    self._ui.set_current_step(SyncStep.RUN_JOBS, job.name, substep=substep)
                    started_at = datetime.now(UTC)
                    try:
                        # Labels this job's executor traffic in the debug trace (#210) and
                        # in the --confirm-each-command prompt. Set per job rather than per
                        # executor because the executors are shared by every job.
                        with active_job(job.name):
                            await job.execute()
                        ended_at = datetime.now(UTC)
                        results.append(
                            JobResult(
                                job_name=job.name,
                                status=JobStatus.SUCCESS,
                                started_at=started_at,
                                ended_at=ended_at,
                            )
                        )
                        self._logger.info(
                            "Job %s completed successfully",
                            job.name,
                            extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": "source"},
                        )

                    except SyncAbortedByUser:
                        # A job-level declined confirmation (e.g. FolderSyncJob's
                        # first-sync overwrite gate via the shared confirmer) is
                        # expected control flow, not a job failure. Let it pass
                        # through untouched so run() logs it once at WARNING and
                        # records an ABORTED session, rather than a spurious
                        # FAILED job result plus a duplicate CRITICAL log.
                        raise
                    except PackageItemFailures as e:
                        # The user approved changes across several package managers in
                        # ONE batched review (D-24); letting one manager's failed items
                        # cancel another manager's already-approved work would silently
                        # break that promise. Record this job's FAILED result (D-27) but
                        # deliberately do NOT re-raise, so the remaining jobs still run —
                        # every other exception keeps today's abort-the-run behavior.
                        ended_at = datetime.now(UTC)
                        results.append(
                            JobResult(
                                job_name=job.name,
                                status=JobStatus.FAILED,
                                started_at=started_at,
                                ended_at=ended_at,
                                error_message=str(e),
                            )
                        )
                        self._logger.critical(
                            "Job %s failed: %s",
                            job.name,
                            e,
                            extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": "source"},
                        )
                    except Exception as e:
                        ended_at = datetime.now(UTC)
                        results.append(
                            JobResult(
                                job_name=job.name,
                                status=JobStatus.FAILED,
                                started_at=started_at,
                                ended_at=ended_at,
                                error_message=str(e),
                            )
                        )
                        self._logger.critical(
                            "Job %s failed: %s",
                            job.name,
                            e,
                            extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": "source"},
                        )
                        # Already reported with the job name; stop run()'s top-level
                        # handler from logging the identical cause a second time.
                        _mark_failure_logged(e)
                        raise
            finally:
                # Cancel monitor tasks so TaskGroup can exit
                # Monitors run forever (while True loop), so they must be cancelled
                source_monitor_task.cancel()
                target_monitor_task.cancel()

    async def _run_snap_hold_command(self, host: Host, cmd: str, *, mutates: str | None = None) -> CommandResult:
        """Run a snap-hold command on `host`, honoring each executor's shell contract.

        The source is the local executor (no login-shell notion — its `run_command` takes
        no `login_shell`); the target is the remote executor, invoked with
        `login_shell=False` to match snap_sync's own target calls. Callers only reach here
        after the hold is engaged, which happens post-connect, so both executors are set.

        `mutates` is passed straight through: the capture (`snap get`) is a read and leaves
        it None, while applying and restoring the hold are system writes on both machines
        and name themselves, so `--confirm-each-command` shows them like any other change.
        """
        if host is Host.SOURCE:
            assert self._local_executor is not None
            return await self._local_executor.run_command(cmd, mutates=mutates)
        assert self._remote_executor is not None
        return await self._remote_executor.run_command(cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=mutates)

    async def _capture_snap_hold(self, host: Host) -> str | None:
        """Read `host`'s current system-wide snap `refresh.hold` (read-only).

        Returns the raw value — an RFC3339 timestamp or the literal `forever` — when a hold
        is set, or None when none is (snap exits non-zero, or prints nothing, for an unset
        option). Never mutates: `snap get` is the same read-only verb snap_sync.validate uses.
        """
        result = await self._run_snap_hold_command(host, "snap get system refresh.hold")
        value = result.stdout.strip()
        return value if result.success and value else None

    async def _apply_snap_hold(self, host: Host) -> None:
        """Set a timed system-wide `refresh.hold` on `host` (best-effort).

        Writes `now + _SNAP_AUTOREFRESH_HOLD_DURATION` (computed on the host) via
        `sudo snap set system refresh.hold=...`. A failure is logged, not raised: pausing
        auto-refresh is a best-effort race guard, and failing the whole sync because it could
        not be set would be worse than proceeding without it (validate() has already
        confirmed snap + passwordless sudo on both hosts).
        """
        cmd = f'sudo snap set system refresh.hold="$({_SNAP_HOLD_TIMESTAMP_CMD})"'
        result = await self._run_snap_hold_command(host, cmd, mutates="pause snapd auto-refresh for the sync window")
        if not result.success:
            self._logger.warning(
                "Could not pause snapd auto-refresh on %s: %s",
                host.value,
                result.stderr.strip(),
                extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": host.value},

        snap_sync performs.

            return

        self._snap_hold_prior_source = await self._capture_snap_hold(Host.SOURCE)
        self._snap_hold_prior_target = await self._capture_snap_hold(Host.TARGET)
        # Engage BEFORE applying so a partially-applied hold is still restored in _cleanup.
        self._snap_hold_engaged = True
        self._logger.info(
            "Pausing snapd auto-refresh on both hosts for the sync window",
            extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": "source"},

        await self._apply_snap_hold(Host.SOURCE)
        await self._apply_snap_hold(Host.TARGET)

        """Restore `host`'s `refresh.hold` to its pre-sync value, or unset it (best-effort).

        When a prior hold was captured it is written back verbatim (an RFC3339 timestamp or
        `forever`); when there was none, `refresh.hold` is set empty, which snapd treats as
        no hold — leaving any unrelated per-snap holds untouched.

        Gated by `--confirm-each-command` like every other modification. Restoring is not
        merely lifting: when a prior hold was captured, skipping this write means the timed
        hold pc-switcher set expires and the user's OWN hold is gone with it — which is why
        the gate description names the value being written back.

        hold self-expires) but never a DECLINED one: `SyncAbortedByUser` is re-raised ahead
        of the broad handler, because a user answering "abort" is a decision to honor, not
        an error to absorb. `_cleanup` decides how far that abort travels.

            description = f"restore this machine's own snapd refresh.hold ({prior}), which this run overwrote"
        else:
            cmd = 'sudo snap set system refresh.hold=""'
            description = "clear the snapd refresh.hold this run set"
        try:
            result = await self._run_snap_hold_command(host, cmd, mutates=description)
            if not result.success:

                    host.value,
                    result.stderr.strip(),
                    extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": host.value},
                )

# Phase 02 — package sync scenario/coverage matrix

Requirement-derived scenario enumeration for the four package jobs, mapped to pytest coverage. Branches come from ADR-020, 02-CONTEXT.md (D-01…D-33), 02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md and docs/jobs/package-sync.md — not from code paths, though code was read to decide what actually happens.

## Legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| U | covered by a unit test that asserts this branch |
| V | covered by the VM integration suite |
| P | partial — a neighbouring test exists, this branch is not asserted |
| — | no coverage |
| ‼ | verified defect or verified requirement gap (probed this session) |

Test file shorthand: `apt` = tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py · `snap` = test_snap_sync.py · `flat` = test_flatpak_sync.py · `man` = test_manual_installs_sync.py · `core` = test_package_sync_core.py · `rev` = test_package_review.py · `state` = test_package_state.py · `items` = test_package_items.py · `fold` = test_folder_sync.py · `hold` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_snap_autorefresh_hold.py · `gate` = tests/unit/test_step_gate.py · `cfg` = tests/unit/orchestrator/test_config_system.py · `exit` = test_session_status_from_job_results.py · `INT` = tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py

## A. apt packages — presence and version diff (D-03, D-04, D-25)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | On source's manual set, absent on target, candidate exists | MISSING_ON_TARGET → INSTALL, default-ticked | U V | core:`test_missing_on_target_yields_install`, apt:`test_diff_yields_exactly_two_missing_items`, INT:`test_apt_sync_installs_missing_package` |
| A2 | On source, absent on target, target repos offer no candidate | REPO_UNAVAILABLE → REPORT_ONLY, never an install | U | core:`test_missing_and_unavailable_yields_repo_unavailable_not_install`, apt:`test_no_candidate_package_is_reported_not_installed` |
| A3 | On target's manual set only | EXTRA_ON_TARGET → REMOVE, own unticked group | U | core:`test_extra_on_target_yields_remove`, apt:`test_extra_on_target_yields_extra_on_target_remove` |
| A4 | Present both, equal version | no diff at all | U | core:`test_equal_versions_yields_no_diff` |
| A5 | Present both, versions differ | VERSION_MISMATCH → REPORT_ONLY naming both versions; never force-converged | U | core:`test_version_mismatch_yields_report_only_with_both_versions` |
| A6 | Version ordering (epoch, tilde, revision) | decided by `dpkg --compare-versions`, never string compare | U | items:`TestCompareDebVersions` (incl. real-dpkg cross-check) |
| A7 | Package pinned on target via preferences.d | HELD_OR_PINNED REPORT_ONLY echo on the package | U | core:`test_pin_fact_yields_held_or_pinned_distinguishable_from_a_hold_item`, apt:`test_preferences_d_pin_surfaces_with_pin_mechanism_and_filename` |
| A8 | Package held on target | install/upgrade action suppressed, no package-level report | U | core:`test_target_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_remove_and_suppresses_package_action`, apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| A9 | Package pinned *and* a hold exists for another package | pin echo and hold item coexist, stay distinguishable | U | apt:`test_pin_still_yields_report_only_echo_alongside_a_hold_item` |
| A10 | Dependency-only package (not in `apt-mark showmanual`) | never in the manifest → never installed, never removed, never reported | P | implicit in capture (`showmanual` only); no test asserts an auto-installed package is invisible. **This is the mechanism the user's example 1 depends on.** |
| A11 | Same package is no-candidate on source *and* missing on target | surfaces twice: `manual_installs_sync` unreproducible item + `apt_sync` REPO_UNAVAILABLE report | — | no test; two managers describe one package in two reviews |
| A12 | `apt-mark showmanual` empty on a machine | empty manifest, no crash, no mass removal | P | `_resolve_versions` early-returns; no test for the empty-source→remove-everything shape |
| A13 | Version resolution source | `dpkg-query`, never `apt list --installed` | U | apt:`test_dpkg_query_used_not_apt_list_installed` |

## B. apt holds (#208 D1–D6)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Held on source, not target | `apt:hold:<pkg>` INSTALL → `sudo apt-mark hold` | U | apt:`test_source_held_yields_install_hold_item_and_converge_runs_apt_mark_hold`, core:`test_source_hold_only_yields_apt_hold_install` |
| B2 | Held on target, not source | REMOVE → `sudo apt-mark unhold`, unticked removal group | U | apt:`test_target_held_only_yields_remove_unhold_item` |
| B3 | Held on both / neither | no hold diff | U | apt:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_hold_diff`, core:`test_held_on_both_yields_no_diff` |
| B4 | Hold identity is distinct from package identity | two separate review items for one package | U | apt:`test_held_package_yields_hold_item_not_duplicate_held_or_pinned_report` |
| B5 | Review verb | group/entry read "hold"/"unhold", never "install"/"remove" | — | **no test asserts the group title or `action_label` for APT_HOLD/SNAP_HOLD/FLATPAK_MASK** — the crux of #208 D3 |
| B6 | Hold converges after the package install in the same run (D8) | install lands before its hold | — | snap has the equivalent test; apt does not |
| B7 | Hold approved for a package whose install was skipped (D6) | `apt-mark hold` on an absent package → normal per-item failure | — | no test; actual `apt-mark` exit behaviour for an unknown package unverified |
| B8 | skip-always on a hold item | DecisionEntry written on the holder's machine | U | apt:`test_skip_always_on_a_hold_writes_the_decision_file` |
| B9 | skip-always on a hold item, next run | item inert, no diff | ‼ | **BROKEN — verified.** `collect_hold_sets()` output never passes `filter_inert`, so the hold diff is re-emitted every run despite the recorded decision |
| B10 | Holds drive no `apt-get -s` simulation | selection state only | P | code filters to APT_PACKAGE; no test |
| B11 | `/usr/bin/apt-mark` in the target sudo grant | named in the hint | U | apt:`test_apt_mark_is_in_the_target_sudo_command_list` |

## C. apt repository config — sources, keys, pins, apt.conf (D-11, D-12, D-13, D-27)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Source file missing on target, key present on source | INSTALL | U | apt:`test_source_with_key_present_on_source_yields_plain_install` |
| C2 | Source file whose `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` names a key absent on the source | REPORT_ONLY + dangling detail, never installable | U | apt:`test_source_with_dangling_keyring_reference_is_flagged_not_installable` |
| C3 | Same, but the source file is *changed* rather than missing | also downgraded to REPORT_ONLY | U | apt:`test_changed_source_with_dangling_keyring_reference_is_downgraded_to_report_only` |
| C4 | deb822 `.sources` vs legacy `.list` | format recorded per file, never normalised; identity is the filename | U | apt:`test_deb822_and_legacy_source_each_record_own_format` |
| C5 | Same repo described by both a `.list` and a `.sources` file | two distinct items, both visible | P | identity-by-filename tested; the coexistence case itself is not |
| C6 | Key present per-repo vs global-trust with the same filename | distinct item ids | U | apt:`test_per_repo_and_global_trust_keys_are_distinct_item_ids` |
| C7 | Key digests identical on both machines | no diff, no content fetch | U | apt:`test_key_matching_digest_on_both_sides_produces_no_diff` |
| C8 | Key content differs | VERSION_MISMATCH → CHANGE, bytes copied verbatim | P | diff shape covered by `_diff_apt_keys`; no test converges a *changed* key |
| C9 | Pin/config file missing / extra / changed | INSTALL / REMOVE / CHANGE | U | apt:`test_pin_and_config_diff_missing_extra_and_changed` |
| C10 | Convergence order | key → pin/config → source → `apt-get update` → packages | U | apt:`test_key_then_source_then_update_then_package_install` |
| C11 | Several repo items approved | exactly one `apt-get update` | U | apt:`test_apt_get_update_runs_exactly_once_for_three_repo_items` |
| C12 | Keys never re-fetched from a vendor | no command contains a URL | U | apt:`test_no_key_command_contains_a_url` |
| C13 | Key write fails | dependent source file left unwritten | U | apt:`test_failed_key_write_leaves_dependent_source_unwritten` |
| C14 | `/etc/apt` write mechanism | stage under `~/.cache`, `sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644`, never `mv`, never `send_file` outside home | U | apt:`test_promotion_uses_sudo_install_with_owner_group_mode_never_mv`, `test_send_file_destinations_start_with_home_never_contain_etc` |
| C15 | Staging copy lifecycle | removed on success and on failure | U | apt:`test_staging_file_removed_after_success_and_after_failure` |
| C16 | `/etc/apt/keyrings` absent (fresh 24.04) | `sudo mkdir -p -m 0755` before `install` | U | apt:`test_promotion_ensures_keyrings_directory_before_install` |
| C17 | Directory preparation fails | fails that item only, not the run | U | apt:`test_directory_preparation_failure_fails_the_item_not_the_run` |
| C18 | Repo file extra on target | single `sudo rm -f` naming that file | U | apt:`test_remove_source_issues_single_rm_naming_that_file` |
| C19 | `apt-get update` fails after the group's writes | back up → restore changed → delete created → every group item recorded FAILED | U | apt:`test_failed_update_restores_changed_deletes_created_records_group_failures` |
| C20 | A rollback step itself fails | named in the summary, backup dir kept | U | apt:`test_failed_rollback_step_warns_and_keeps_the_backup` |
| C21 | `apt-get update` succeeds | no restore command issued, backup discarded | U | apt:`test_successful_update_issues_no_restore_command` |
| C22 | Rollback happened | package items still attempted (D-27) | U | apt:`test_rollback_does_not_prevent_package_items_from_being_attempted` |
| C23 | Backup itself fails | every group item fails, no `KeyError` crash | U | apt:`test_backup_failure_fails_every_group_item_without_crashing` |
| C24 | Source file *and* its key both extra on target, both approved | both deleted, one `apt-get update` after both writes | — | untested; order is key-first for removals too, so a failed source-removal leaves a dangling-key repo when the update runs |
| C25 | Content reads for hydration use sudo | matches the `sudo find … sha256sum` privilege | U | apt:`test_content_hydration_reads_use_sudo_matching_the_digest_capture` |
| C26 | Target has a repo/key the source lacks, still needed by a target-side machine-specific package | removal offered with no awareness of that dependency | ‼ | no linkage exists in the code; see §Q3 (user example 3) |

## D. apt collateral (D-30) and metadata refresh (decision 1)

| # | Scenario | Expected | Cov | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Approved installs, simulation removes an auto-installed package | proceeds silently, no review item | U | apt:`test_auto_collateral_removal_produces_no_review_item`, `test_install_whose_only_collateral_is_auto_deps_proceeds` |
| D2 | Simulation removes a target-manual package | own COLLATERAL group item naming the trigger | U | apt:`test_manual_collateral_removal_becomes_a_collateral_review_item` |
| D3 | Simulation removes a source-manual-only package | protected too (union of both manual sets) | U | apt:`test_source_only_manual_collateral_removal_becomes_a_review_item` |

Flatpak masks are correct, which makes this an asymmetry between the three managers #208 D3 says are uniform.
2. **skip-always on any REPORT_ONLY item records nothing** (H7). - **F21** — a remote removed while a target ref still uses it.
- **C24** — source and its key both removed in one run.
- **L10** — the VM check #208 D9 explicitly promised for the per-snap-hold capture-timing assumption.
- **A10/N8** — auto-installed dependencies are invisible to the manifest; the safety of the whole apt model rests on it and no test states it.
- **M12** — `--confirm-each-command` refused without a TTY.
- **I22/N11** — real-TTY review rendering and the two-machine walkthrough remain UAT-only.

## Findings

Verified defects (probed this session against the real code):

1. **skip-always never silences an apt or snap hold** (B9, E15). `AptSyncJob.collect_hold_sets()` output and `snap_sync._diff_snap_holds`'s inputs bypass `filter_inert`, and `filter_inert` matches `snap:<name>`, not `snap:hold:<name>`. The decision file entry is written (there is a test for the write) and then ignored forever — the hold item reappears in every subsequent review. Flatpak masks are correct, which makes this an asymmetry between the three managers #208 D3 says are uniform.
2. **skip-always on any REPORT_ONLY item records nothing** (H7). Version mismatches, repo-unavailable packages and pin echoes are offered the standard three-way choice, and "skip always" silently does nothing — `_record_permanent_skips` filters to INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE. The user cannot make a permanently-mismatched version or an unavailable package stop being reported.

57	await self.target.send_file(local, remote, mutates="push the snippet registry")   # write

<result>Verified. Cleaning up isn't needed (probes live in scratchpad, not the repo tree).

## Verdict

| Manager | Verdict |
|---|---|
| apt (`apt:hold:<pkg>`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| snap (`snap:hold:<name>`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| flatpak (`flatpak:mask:<scope>:<pattern>`) | **REFUTED** (control behaves correctly) |

Both directions (hold/INSTALL and unhold/REMOVE) are broken, on both managers. I could not find any compensating mechanism.

## What I verified

`_record_permanent_skips` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:625-640`) writes `item_id=diff.item_id` verbatim, i.e. `apt:hold:vim` / `snap:hold:foo`, to the correct machine per D-08a (source for INSTALL, target for REMOVE). I confirmed the exact `printf ... mv -f` payload in both directions. So the id written is the hold identity — and nothing on a later run ever looks that id up.

Defect sites:

- apt: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:467` — `source_hold_names, target_hold_names = await self.collect_hold_sets()` bypasses `filter_inert` entirely; those raw sets go straight into `_diff_apt_holds` (`sync_core.py:367`, `sync_core.py:371-393`). `AptSyncJob.collect_hold_sets` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/apt_sync.py:625-634`) re-reads `apt-mark showhold` on both machines each run.
- snap: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py:379-380` filters `SnapItem`s whose `item_id` is `snap:<name>` (`items.py:414`), while the hold identity built by `_hold_diff` is `snap:hold:<name>` (`snap_sync.py:198`). `_diff_snap_holds` (`snap_sync.py:204-224`) derives holds from the surviving items' `.held` flag, so the decision entry can never match.
- flatpak is correct because a mask is a real item (`FlatpakMaskItem.item_id == flatpak:mask:<scope>:<pattern>`, `items.py:495`) passed through `filter_inert` at `src/pcswitcher/jobs/flatpak_sync.py:560-561`.

Adversarial checks that came up empty: no filtering in `review_items` / `_render_group_panel` (`packages/review.py`), none in `_build_review_groups`, none in `AptSyncJob.accept_review` (which explicitly re-buckets `APT_HOLD` diffs to converge last, so it preserves them), none in `orchestrator.py` or `step_gate.py` (neither touches decisions), and `_record_permanent_skips` writes exactly the id the diff carries — no id mismatch that could accidentally match something else.

## Minimal repro (probe, both fail)

Two `plan()` runs with the same mocked machines; run 2's source decision file contains the id written by run 1.

- apt: source `apt-mark showhold` → `vim`, target → empty; decision file holds `apt:hold:vim`. Run 2 still emits `ItemDiff(item_id="apt:hold:vim", APT_HOLD, INSTALL)`.
- snap: source `snap list --all` Notes column `held`, target `-`; decision file holds `snap:hold:foo`. Run 2 still emits `snap:hold:foo`.
- Remove direction (recorded on target) is identically broken; the re-emitted item reaches the review as group `("Unhold apt packages", "unhold", "apt:hold:vim")` / `("Unhold snap packages", "unhold", "snap:hold:foo")`.
- Flatpak control passes: mask disappears from run 2's diffs and groups.

Existing coverage `tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py:656` (`test_skip_always_on_a_hold_writes_the_decision_file`) asserts only the write, never the read-back — which is why this slipped through.

## User-visible consequence (real)

"Skip always" on a hold/unhold is a no-op beyond writing a file nobody reads. Every subsequent sync re-offers the same item. The remove direction reappears in its own unticked "Unhold …" group (recurring noise). The **add** direction is worse: `install` is not a removal action (`review.py:92`), so the re-offered hold comes back **default-checked** every run — a user who bulk-accepts the install group applies the very hold they permanently declined. Contradicts `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md` D3 ("skip-always writes the machine-local `DecisionFile` and `filter_inert` drops it next run") and ADR-020 D-08/D-08a.

## Candidate fixes (not implemented)

**A. Filter the hold sets/flags at their own source.** apt: in `plan()`, drop `n` from `source_hold_names` when `apt:hold:{n}` is in `source_decisions` (same for target). snap: have `_diff_snap_holds` take the two decision maps and skip a name whose `snap:hold:<name>` is recorded.
Trade-off: keeps D-08's "inert at the diff-input boundary" framing, but for apt it needs **two** target-hold sets — `target_hold_names` also suppresses a held package's own install/upgrade action at `sync_core.py:313`, and filtering that set for inertness would re-propose upgrades of a held package. Easy to get subtly wrong; also duplicates the rule per manager.

**B. One shared post-diff inert filter (recommended).** Add a helper on `PackageSyncJob` — e.g. `_drop_inert_diffs(diffs, source_decisions, target_decisions)` — dropping any `ItemDiff` whose `item_id` is recorded on the machine that holds it, using exactly `_record_permanent_skips`'s D-08a rule (INSTALL/CHANGE → source file, REMOVE → target file). Call it at the tail of all three `plan()`s.
Trade-off: filters at review-input rather than diff-input, so `sync_core.py`'s module docstring claim ("made real at the diff-input boundary rather than as a later filter on the review") needs rewording — though that claim is already false for these classes. Upside: one definition, covers apt + snap + any future membership item, leaves the target-hold suppression untouched, and is symmetric with the write path by construction. Since snap/flatpak override `plan()`, the call has to be added in each of the three `plan()`s (or a shared tail extracted).</result>

<result># Verdict: LATENT-ONLY — the claim as written is REFUTED, but it sits on top of a real, broader doc-vs-code gap

## 1. Mechanism: confirmed, exactly as claimed

Throwaway pytest probe (4 tests, all passed, since deleted) against `AptSyncJob` with `make_context`:

- Plan with four diffs (VERSION_MISMATCH, REPO_UNAVAILABLE, HELD_OR_PINNED, MISSING_ON_TARGET/INSTALL), all decided `SKIP_ALWAYS`, `was_interactive=True`.
- Exactly **one** decision-file write reached an executor — the INSTALL item (`pkg-d`). The three `REPORT_ONLY` items produced **zero** writes.

Cause is the guard at `/home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher/src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:628`:

```python
if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
    continue
```

So the dead branch is real at the API level.

## 2. Reachability: no interactive path can produce SKIP_ALWAYS on an apt/snap/flatpak REPORT_ONLY item

- **Checkbox path** — `_build_review_groups` (`sync_core.py:395`) sets `ReviewGroup.action = diff.action.value`, i.e. literally `"report_only"` for these classes. Probe confirmed: apt version-mismatch / repo-unavailable / held-or-pinned collapse into one group with `action == "report_only"`, which matches neither `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` nor `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION`, so `review_items` takes the plain `questionary.checkbox` branch (`review.py:424-445`). I drove the real `review_items` with `questionary.select` patched to raise: it was never called, and the outcome's decision set was `⊆ {APPLY, SKIP_ONCE}`. The `Decision` enum comment at `review.py:157-161` is accurate.
- **Unreproducible three-way path** (`_review_unreproducible_group`, the *only* UI that emits `SKIP_ALWAYS`) — the group is built solely by `ManualInstallsSyncJob._build_review_groups` (`manual_installs_sync.py:464`), and only from diffs with `item_class == UNREPRODUCIBLE`. apt/snap/flatpak never construct such a group.
- **Collateral path** — emits only `APPLY` / `SKIP_ONCE` / abort (`review.py:362-371`).
- **Non-interactive path** — all `SKIP_ONCE`, and `_record_permanent_skips` short-circuits on `was_interactive` anyway.
- **`PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION`** — *is* able to set `SKIP_ALWAYS` on any item id and therefore does hit the dead branch. It is a deliberately undocumented integration-test hatch (`review.py:84-86`, D-26), absent from `--help`, config schema and user docs. Not a user path.

**So no real user is ever offered a permanent-skip choice on a REPORT_ONLY item.** The claim's sting — "offered a choice that silently does nothing" — does not happen.

## 3. Why `manual_installs_sync` is exempt, and whether that's inconsistent

`ManualInstallsSyncJob._finalize_unreproducible` (`manual_installs_sync.py:556-570`) records skip-always for `item_class == UNREPRODUCIBLE` diffs regardless of `action`. Probe confirmed it writes `manual.decisions.yaml` for a `REPORT_ONLY` unreproducible item. It is exempt because it has an unambiguous holder rule the base lacks: unreproducible items are *always* source-held (`self.source`, no target manifest exists — `query_target_items` returns `[]`). The base's D-08a holder rule keys off the converge direction, which `REPORT_ONLY` doesn't have. That's a coherent split, not an accident — but it means the codebase already demonstrates that "REPORT_ONLY has no holder" is a base-class limitation, not a truth about REPORT_ONLY items.

## 4. Requirement check — this is where there *is* a real gap, wider than the claim

- ADR-020 D-07 (`docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md:74`): "Every item class in every job gets a three-way decision: apply / skip once / skip always."
- D-25 puts held/pinned, version-mismatch and repo-unavailable inside that same review.
- `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:40-44` promises the user: "Every item offers the same three-way choice: Apply / Skip this run / **Skip always**."
- `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:107` repeats it for holds/masks: "each with the usual three-way choice — apply, skip this run, or skip always."

The checkbox review offers **two** choices, for *every* item class — not just REPORT_ONLY. Holds and masks (`INSTALL`/`REMOVE`, fully plumbed in `_record_permanent_skips`) are equally unreachable, and `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:107` specifically promises skip-always for them. That is the user-visible defect: **the docs promise a third choice the UI does not render**. The REPORT_ONLY dead branch is a *second* layer that would bite only after the UI gap is closed.

This is already logged as known work: `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md:206` ("the checkbox UI has no path to produce a `SKIP_ALWAYS` outcome for a regular (non-unreproducible) item"), and `.planning/STATE.md:133,146`. Note both reference stale paths (`jobs/package_review.py`, `jobs/package_sync_core.py`); the files are now `jobs/packages/review.py` and `jobs/packages/sync_core.py`.

## Fix approaches (not implemented)

**A. Close the UI gap, then give REPORT_ONLY a holder rule.** Add a post-checkbox "promote any of these skips to permanent?" pass over unticked entries (a second `questionary.checkbox` over the skipped set, or per-item `select`), and replace the `sync_core.py:628` action guard with a `DiffClass`-keyed holder table: `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` → source (only the source has it), `HELD_OR_PINNED` → target (the pin lives there), `UNREPRODUCIBLE` → source (already the manual job's rule, could be folded back into the base). Trade-off: `VERSION_MISMATCH` is genuinely two-sided and has no honest holder — recording it on the source suppresses the package from ever being pushed, which is far stronger than "stop reporting this drift" and would silently disable install/removal sync for that package. That class likely needs a distinct "mute the report" concept rather than a D-08 decision entry.

**B. Don't offer it for REPORT_ONLY; correct the docs.** Close the UI gap for `INSTALL`/`CHANGE`/`REMOVE` only, keep the `sync_core.py:628` guard as the deliberate design it is documented to be, and amend `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:40-44` to scope "every item" to actionable items, noting REPORT_ONLY classes are informational and suppressed by fixing the underlying condition (unpin, add the repo, let versions converge). Cheap and honest, and sidesteps the `VERSION_MISMATCH` holder problem — but it is a partial retreat from ADR-020 D-07 as literally written, so D-07 would need an amending note.

Either way, the guard's docstring at `sync_core.py:613-614` is currently truthful about intent; nothing there is lying to a user today.</result>

<result>Verified. Cleaning up isn't needed (probes live in scratchpad, not the repo tree).

## Verdict

| Manager | Verdict |
|---|---|
| apt (`apt:hold:<pkg>`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| snap (`snap:hold:<name>`) | **CONFIRMED** |
| flatpak (`flatpak:mask:<scope>:<pattern>`) | **REFUTED** (control behaves correctly) |

Both directions (hold/INSTALL and unhold/REMOVE) are broken, on both managers. I could not find any compensating mechanism.

## What I verified

`_record_permanent_skips` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:625-640`) writes `item_id=diff.item_id` verbatim, i.e. `apt:hold:vim` / `snap:hold:foo`, to the correct machine per D-08a (source for INSTALL, target for REMOVE). I confirmed the exact `printf ... mv -f` payload in both directions. So the id written is the hold identity — and nothing on a later run ever looks that id up.

Defect sites:

- apt: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:467` — `source_hold_names, target_hold_names = await self.collect_hold_sets()` bypasses `filter_inert` entirely; those raw sets go straight into `_diff_apt_holds` (`sync_core.py:367`, `sync_core.py:371-393`). `AptSyncJob.collect_hold_sets` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/apt_sync.py:625-634`) re-reads `apt-mark showhold` on both machines each run.
- snap: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py:379-380` filters `SnapItem`s whose `item_id` is `snap:<name>` (`items.py:414`), while the hold identity built by `_hold_diff` is `snap:hold:<name>` (`snap_sync.py:198`). `_diff_snap_holds` (`snap_sync.py:204-224`) derives holds from the surviving items' `.held` flag, so the decision entry can never match.
- flatpak is correct because a mask is a real item (`FlatpakMaskItem.item_id == flatpak:mask:<scope>:<pattern>`, `items.py:495`) passed through `filter_inert` at `src/pcswitcher/jobs/flatpak_sync.py:560-561`.

Adversarial checks that came up empty: no filtering in `review_items` / `_render_group_panel` (`packages/review.py`), none in `_build_review_groups`, none in `AptSyncJob.accept_review` (which explicitly re-buckets `APT_HOLD` diffs to converge last, so it preserves them), none in `orchestrator.py` or `step_gate.py` (neither touches decisions), and `_record_permanent_skips` writes exactly the id the diff carries — no id mismatch that could accidentally match something else.

## Minimal repro (probe, both fail)

Two `plan()` runs with the same mocked machines; run 2's source decision file contains the id written by run 1.

- apt: source `apt-mark showhold` → `vim`, target → empty; decision file holds `apt:hold:vim`. Run 2 still emits `ItemDiff(item_id="apt:hold:vim", APT_HOLD, INSTALL)`.
- snap: source `snap list --all` Notes column `held`, target `-`; decision file holds `snap:hold:foo`. Run 2 still emits `snap:hold:foo`.
- Remove direction (recorded on target) is identically broken; the re-emitted item reaches the review as group `("Unhold apt packages", "unhold", "apt:hold:vim")` / `("Unhold snap packages", "unhold", "snap:hold:foo")`.
- Flatpak control passes: mask disappears from run 2's diffs and groups.

Existing coverage `tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py:656` (`test_skip_always_on_a_hold_writes_the_decision_file`) asserts only the write, never the read-back — which is why this slipped through.

## User-visible consequence (real)

"Skip always" on a hold/unhold is a no-op beyond writing a file nobody reads. Every subsequent sync re-offers the same item. The remove direction reappears in its own unticked "Unhold …" group (recurring noise). The **add** direction is worse: `install` is not a removal action (`review.py:92`), so the re-offered hold comes back **default-checked** every run — a user who bulk-accepts the install group applies the very hold they permanently declined. Contradicts `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md` D3 ("skip-always writes the machine-local `DecisionFile` and `filter_inert` drops it next run") and ADR-020 D-08/D-08a.

## Candidate fixes (not implemented)

**A. Filter the hold sets/flags at their own source.** apt: in `plan()`, drop `n` from `source_hold_names` when `apt:hold:{n}` is in `source_decisions` (same for target). snap: have `_diff_snap_holds` take the two decision maps and skip a name whose `snap:hold:<name>` is recorded.
Trade-off: keeps D-08's "inert at the diff-input boundary" framing, but for apt it needs **two** target-hold sets — `target_hold_names` also suppresses a held package's own install/upgrade action at `sync_core.py:313`, and filtering that set for inertness would re-propose upgrades of a held package. Easy to get subtly wrong; also duplicates the rule per manager.

**B. One shared post-diff inert filter (recommended).** Add a helper on `PackageSyncJob` — e.g. `_drop_inert_diffs(diffs, source_decisions, target_decisions)` — dropping any `ItemDiff` whose `item_id` is recorded on the machine that holds it, using exactly `_record_permanent_skips`'s D-08a rule (INSTALL/CHANGE → source file, REMOVE → target file). Call it at the tail of all three `plan()`s.
Trade-off: filters at review-input rather than diff-input, so `sync_core.py`'s module docstring claim ("made real at the diff-input boundary rather than as a later filter on the review") needs rewording — though that claim is already false for these classes. Upside: one definition, covers apt + snap + any future membership item, leaves the target-hold suppression untouched, and is symmetric with the write path by construction. Since snap/flatpak override `plan()`, the call has to be added in each of the three `plan()`s (or a shared tail extracted).</result>

<result># Verdict: LATENT-ONLY — the claim as written is REFUTED, but it sits on top of a real, broader doc-vs-code gap

## 1. Mechanism: confirmed, exactly as claimed

Throwaway pytest probe (4 tests, all passed, since deleted) against `AptSyncJob` with `make_context`:

- Plan with four diffs (VERSION_MISMATCH, REPO_UNAVAILABLE, HELD_OR_PINNED, MISSING_ON_TARGET/INSTALL), all decided `SKIP_ALWAYS`, `was_interactive=True`.
- Exactly **one** decision-file write reached an executor — the INSTALL item (`pkg-d`). The three `REPORT_ONLY` items produced **zero** writes.

Cause is the guard at `/home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher/src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py:628`:

```python
if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
    continue
```

So the dead branch is real at the API level.

## 2. Reachability: no interactive path can produce SKIP_ALWAYS on an apt/snap/flatpak REPORT_ONLY item

- **Checkbox path** — `_build_review_groups` (`sync_core.py:395`) sets `ReviewGroup.action = diff.action.value`, i.e. literally `"report_only"` for these classes. Probe confirmed: apt version-mismatch / repo-unavailable / held-or-pinned collapse into one group with `action == "report_only"`, which matches neither `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` nor `COLLATERAL_REVIEW_ACTION`, so `review_items` takes the plain `questionary.checkbox` branch (`review.py:424-445`). I drove the real `review_items` with `questionary.select` patched to raise: it was never called, and the outcome's decision set was `⊆ {APPLY, SKIP_ONCE}`. The `Decision` enum comment at `review.py:157-161` is accurate.
- **Unreproducible three-way path** (`_review_unreproducible_group`, the *only* UI that emits `SKIP_ALWAYS`) — the group is built solely by `ManualInstallsSyncJob._build_review_groups` (`manual_installs_sync.py:464`), and only from diffs with `item_class == UNREPRODUCIBLE`. apt/snap/flatpak never construct such a group.
- **Collateral path** — emits only `APPLY` / `SKIP_ONCE` / abort (`review.py:362-371`).
- **Non-interactive path** — all `SKIP_ONCE`, and `_record_permanent_skips` short-circuits on `was_interactive` anyway.
- **`PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION`** — *is* able to set `SKIP_ALWAYS` on any item id and therefore does hit the dead branch. It is a deliberately undocumented integration-test hatch (`review.py:84-86`, D-26), absent from `--help`, config schema and user docs. Not a user path.

**So no real user is ever offered a permanent-skip choice on a REPORT_ONLY item.** The claim's sting — "offered a choice that silently does nothing" — does not happen.

## 3. Why `manual_installs_sync` is exempt, and whether that's inconsistent

- snap: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py:379-380` filters `SnapItem`s whose `item_id` is `snap:<name>`, but the hold identity is `snap:hold:<name>` (`snap_sync.py:198`), so the recorded entry can never match. `_diff_snap_holds` is at `snap_sync.py:204-224`.
- flatpak masks are CORRECT (`flatpak_sync.py:560-561` passes real `FlatpakMaskItem`s through `filter_inert`) — this is the positive control; do not break it.
- `_record_permanent_skips` (`sync_core.py:625-640`) writes `diff.item_id` verbatim to the machine that holds the item per D-08a: INSTALL/CHANGE → source file, REMOVE → target file.

Consequence, worst part: the ADD direction re-appears **default-checked** (`review.py:92` — `install` is not a removal action), so a user who bulk-accepts the install group applies the very hold they permanently declined. Violates `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-208-HOLD-MASK-REPLICATION.md` D3 and ADR-020 D-08/D-08a.

Implement the shared post-diff filter (this approach was chosen deliberately — do not substitute a per-manager fix):

Add a helper on `PackageSyncJob` (e.g. `_drop_inert_diffs(diffs, source_decisions, target_decisions)`) that drops any `ItemDiff` whose `item_id` is recorded on the machine that holds it, applying EXACTLY the same D-08a rule `_record_permanent_skips` uses (INSTALL/CHANGE → source decisions, REMOVE → target decisions). Call it at the tail of the diff step in all four `plan()` implementations (base `sync_core.py`, plus the overrides in `apt_sync.py`, `snap_sync.py`, `flatpak_sync.py`) — or extract a shared tail if that is cleaner. The write path and the read path must be symmetric by construction.

TRAP you must not fall into: for apt, `target_hold_names` does double duty — besides driving the hold diff it also SUPPRESSES a held package's own install/upgrade action at `sync_core.py:313`. Filtering that set for inertness would wrongly re-propose upgrades of a held package. That is precisely why the filter belongs AFTER the diff, on `ItemDiff`s, not on the input sets. Verify this by test.

Also: `sync_core.py`'s module docstring currently claims inertness is "made real at the diff-input boundary rather than as a later filter on the review". That claim is now false for these classes — update the docstring to describe what the code actually does, and say why (membership items derive from state that has no item-level identity to filter on the way in). Keep it terse, per the repo's writing style. Do not add history or narrate the change.

Cover, for apt AND snap, both directions (hold INSTALL recorded on source; unhold REMOVE recorded on target): run 1 records, run 2 emits no such diff and no such review group. Include the flatpak mask positive control (still filtered). Include the apt trap regression: a package held on the target still has its install/upgrade action suppressed even when some unrelated hold decision is recorded. Follow the existing test style; `make_context` in tests/unit/jobs/test_apt_sync.py is importable and other test modules already import from each other. The decision file is read via a `cat ~/...` command you can stub; YAML shape is in `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/state.py`.

`uv run ruff format . && uv run ruff check . && uv run basedpyright && uv run pytest tests/unit -q` — all clean. If another agent's concurrent commit breaks your run, re-run; do not "fix" their tests.

Two atomic commits: the src fix (`fix(02): honour skip-always for apt and snap block-state items`) and the tests, or one combined commit if the repo's convention prefers that — check `git log --oneline -20` for how fix+test commits are paired in this phase and follow it. Include the repo's required trailers (copy the format from `git log -1 --format=%B`). Reference that this closes the #208 D3 gap.

Close a confirmed code-vs-docs gap: the batched checkbox review offers only TWO outcomes (apply / skip once) for every regular item, while ADR-020 D-07 and `docs/jobs/package-sync.md` promise a three-way choice including "skip always".

## Ownership — several agents are working concurrently

You own: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py`, `docs/jobs/package-sync.md`, `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md`, `.planning/codebase/CONCERNS.md`, `.planning/STATE.md`, and a NEW test file `tests/unit/jobs/test_review_skip_always.py`.

You MUST NOT edit: `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/sync_core.py`, `apt_sync.py`, `snap_sync.py`, `flatpak_sync.py`, `items.py`, `state.py` (another agent is fixing a defect in those), nor any EXISTING test file under tests/ (other agents own them). If you believe a change outside your files is required, STOP and report it instead of making it.

## Scope (decided by the user — implement exactly this)

Offer skip-always for **actionable items only**: diffs whose action is INSTALL, CHANGE or REMOVE — which includes the block-state items (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`, `flatpak:mask:`), for which `docs/jobs/package-sync.md:107` promises it explicitly. REPORT_ONLY items (version mismatch, repo-unavailable, held/pinned echo) stay informational and are NOT offered skip-always: a version drift has no honest "holder" machine, and recording one would silently stop that package syncing altogether — much stronger than "stop reporting this".

## Requirements for the implementation

Read `src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py` fully first, plus `_record_permanent_skips` in sync_core.py (read only — do not edit) to see what the write path already accepts. `Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS` and its persistence already exist and work for actionable items; only the UI path to produce it is missing.

- Add the third choice to the ordinary checkbox flow. A reasonable shape: after a group's checkbox returns, run a second prompt over the UNTICKED entries of that group asking which should be permanent ("never offer this again on this machine"). Choose the interaction you judge best within the existing questionary + Rich Live constraints — but it must not turn the review back into a per-item question queue (D-24: the user wants to tick items off a list). If every entry was ticked, prompt nothing.
- Must compose with everything the module already guarantees: `ui.pause()`/`resume()` in a `finally`, the blocking `.ask()` dispatched via `asyncio.to_thread` (ADR-005), untrusted labels wrapped in `Text` (never bare `str` into a Panel/console — the MarkupError guard).
- Ctrl-C / EOF at the new prompt aborts the WHOLE sync (`SyncAbortedByUser`), consistent with the existing checkbox and unreproducible rules. Never a silent per-item fallthrough.

That's now being implemented for actionable items per your decision.

**Classic snaps — CONFIRMED.** `zellij` on this machine is classic; snapd's refusal is per-*revision*, so `--revision=N` doesn't bypass it. Seven agents: snap/flatpak gap tests **done** (commit `f2c8743e`, 15 tests, no xfails); apt tests, core/state/manual tests, CLI-gate + `mutates=` audit, the hold-skip-always fix, the skip-always review UI, and VM integration tests still running. A **second checkbox per actionable group**, run over only the entries the apply checkbox left unticked: message `"<group title> — never offer again on this machine?"`, all choices unchecked, ticks recorded as `Decision.SKIP_ALWAYS`. A fully-ticked group prompts nothing; an empty second list is exactly today's skip-once behaviour, so a bare Enter is a no-op. Promotions are applied only to ids that were actually offered, so a promotion can never overwrite an `APPLY` already recorded.

## What changed

**`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/items.py`** — `SnapItem` gains `classic: bool = False` and `devmode: bool = False`, defaulted exactly like `held`. Docstring documents why they are fields and not identity: confinement is a store property of the published revision, not something two machines can legitimately disagree about for the same revision, so identity would split one snap into two items and a diff on it would propose a convergence with no command behind it.

**`src/pcswitcher/jobs/snap_sync.py`**
- `_parse_snap_list` reads `classic`/`devmode` from the `notes` list it already splits for `held`/`disabled`.
- New `_confinement_flags(item) -> str` returns a leading-space fragment, at most ONE flag, classic winning over devmode.
- `_converge_install`: `sudo snap install{flags} --revision=N name`.
- `_converge_change` refresh path: `sudo snap refresh{flags} --revision=N name`.
- Diff logic untouched — `_diff_snap_items` still compares revision and channel only.

**`tests/unit/jobs/test_snap_sync.py`** — `TestParseConfinement` (classic fixture, devmode fixture, and a `disabled,classic` line proving `disabled` still wins in the shared Notes list, which is the real `snap list --all` shape on this machine) and `TestConvergeConfinement` (classic install carries `--classic`, strict install carries neither flag, devmode install carries `--devmode` and never `--classic`, refresh carries `--classic` when the target is strict, and a confinement-only difference produces `plan.diffs == ()`).

## Mutual exclusivity — verified

`snap install --help` documents both flags but states no exclusivity. Grepping the 2.76.1 `/usr/bin/snap` binary for `cannot use ...` strings shows the CLI enforces exactly one mode-flag pair: `cannot use devmode and jailmode flags together`. There is no classic+devmode rejection, so a nonsensical pair would be **accepted silently** — which is precisely why `_confinement_flags` emits one or the other, never both. Semantically they request incompatible modes: `--devmode` is documented as relaxing confinement "for strict snaps", `--classic` as confirming a classic-confinement revision.

## The refresh-path question — decided, and verifiable both ways

I **could** verify the underlying claim, and it turned out to point the opposite way from the inference in the brief. `snap refresh --help` on this machine states: *"With no further options, the snaps are refreshed to the current revision of the channel they're tracking, **preserving their confinement options**."* That is real, but it describes the **target's** current confinement — the wrong one exactly in the named case. Source classic + target strict, same snap (a snap that changed confinement between the two installed revisions): a plain refresh preserves the target's *strict*, then hits the same per-revision refusal an install would, because snapd's check is per-revision (`This revision of snap %q was published using classic confinement` — string confirmed in the binary).

So the flag is **always** passed from the SOURCE item on the refresh path, not conditioned on the target. That is also the safe direction: `--classic` where it is not needed is only a warning (`flag --classic ignored for strictly confined snap %s`, confirmed in the binary), while omitting it where it is needed is a hard failure on every run. Rationale is in `_converge_change`'s docstring.

Reverse skew (source strict, target classic) emits no flag and leaves the target's confinement alone — consistent with confinement not being identity and never producing a diff. Also noted in that docstring.

## Verification

- `ruff format` + `ruff check` on my three files only: clean.
- `uv run basedpyright`: 9 errors, **all** in `tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py` (unused imports/functions — another agent's in-flight file). Zero in files I touched. Left alone.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit -q`: 1096 passed, 1 xfailed. All pre-existing snap tests still pass unchanged (the strict-snap command strings they assert are byte-identical, since `_confinement_flags` returns `""`).

## Docs

No change made. I checked `docs/jobs/package-sync.md` for claims about snap install mechanics — it only says snaps are "converged to the source's exact revision and tracking channel" (lines 24, 101) and never claims anything about install flags or confinement. Nothing there became more or less precise, so per your instruction I added no noise.

## Follow-up worth filing

**Sideloaded snaps (`x<N>` revisions) are unhandled and out of scope by decision.** A snap installed from a local `.snap` file gets a store-less revision rendered as `x1`, `x2`, … in `snap list`. `snap_sync` captures that literally and emits `sudo snap install --revision=x1 <name>` on the target, where the store has no such revision to fetch — a permanent per-item failure with no user-actionable review text, structurally the same defect class as the classic bug just fixed. The product decision it needs: which diff class an unfetchable revision gets. Plausible options are `DiffClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE` routed to `manual_installs_sync` (probably the right home — it already owns "things no package manager can reproduce"), or a `REPORT_ONLY` snap diff that names the fact without proposing a command. Detection is cheap (`revision.startswith("x")`). There are **zero** sideloaded snaps on this machine (all 17 have numeric revisions), so this cannot be tested against real state here — that is the main reason it was deferred rather than folded in.</result>

content.text:
Tree is clean — every agent committed, nothing stray left behind. Ten new commits on the branch.

## What landed

**Fixes**
- `3cf963be` + `39112558` — hold skip-always. A shared `_drop_inert_diffs` on `PackageSyncJob` now applies the same D-08a holder rule the write path uses, called at the tail of all four `plan()`s. It also closed a gap I hadn't spotted: apt's *repo* diffs (digest-derived) had the same defect. Proven non-vacuous by stashing `src/` — 7 of 10 new tests fail without it, the 3 flatpak controls pass either way.
- `5cf1d802` + `8fd31820` — skip-always in the review UI. Shape chosen: a **second checkbox per actionable group**, over only the entries the apply checkbox left unticked ("never offer again on this machine?"). Keeps D-24's tick-a-list feel; a fully-ticked group prompts nothing; Ctrl-C there aborts the sync like every other review prompt. ADR-020 got a 2026-07-25 amendment scoping D-07 to actionable items, and the stale `CONCERNS.md`/`STATE.md` entries are corrected.
- `8c2fa02c` — classic/devmode snaps. **The assumption in my brief was wrong and the agent caught it**: `snap refresh` preserves the *target's* confinement, which is exactly backwards for the source-classic/target-strict case, so the flag is now always passed from the source item on both install and refresh. Also found that snapd would silently accept `--classic --devmode` together, so at most one is ever emitted.

**Tests** — 5 commits, ~60 new tests, unit suite now 1096 passing. Only one xfail in the tree: the `mutates=` audit, which is being fixed right now.

## Two things needing your call later

**Sideloaded snaps** (`x1` revisions) are still unhandled — same defect class as classic, structurally: `snap install --revision=x1` can never resolve against the store. Deferred by your decision; it needs a product call on which diff class an unfetchable revision gets (`manual_installs_sync` is probably its real home). Zero instances on this machine, so it can't be tested here.

**Flatpak remote removal orphaning refs** — confirmed, pinned by a test, no guard exists.

Both want GitHub issues; I haven't filed anything.

## Caveats on the VM tests

The 7 integration tests are **written but never executed** — correctly so: the suite installs pc-switcher onto both VMs and takes a global lock, and running it mid-refactor would have tested a half-changed tree. They need a PR against `main` to run at all (integration CI skips stacked PRs). So the `V` marks in the matrix are "written, unverified" until that runs.

The **#208 D9 verdict is still undetermined** — whether a system-wide `refresh.hold` masks per-snap `held` notes. It's now an executable check with failure text that names the consequence, rather than an untested comment.

Waiting on the last agent, then I'll do a clean full verification and update the matrix.

`flatpak_sync` offers a target-only remote for removal with no awareness that installed refs on the target still name it as their origin. Approving the removal orphans those refs.

The dependent ref is frequently installed identically on **both** machines, so it produces no diff at all and never appears in the review. content.text:
Issue **#214** filed for the flatpak remote orphaning. The fix goes out as soon as the running test agent releases `test_flatpak_sync.py` — I'm serializing rather than risking a clobber.

## Sideloaded snaps — what they are and why they break

Normally a snap comes from the Snap Store, and every published revision has a store-assigned number (`zellij` is revision 65 on this machine). But you can also install a snap straight from a local `.snap` file — `snap install --dangerous ./foo.snap`, or `snap try` during development. There's no store revision for that, so snapd assigns a **local** one, rendered with an `x` prefix: `x1`, `x2`, and so on. The `x` literally means "these bytes came from a file, not the store."

pc-switcher captures name + channel + revision from `snap list` on the source, then converges the target with `snap install --revision=<N>`. For a sideloaded snap that becomes:

```
sudo snap install --revision=x1 foo
```

on the target — and the store has no revision `x1` of `foo`, because that revision only ever existed as a file on the source machine's disk. It fails. Every run, forever, with review text that gives the user no hint what to do. Sideloaded snaps also usually track no channel, so the channel switch that follows would be equally meaningless.

It's structurally the same defect as the classic-confinement bug just fixed: captured state turned into a command that cannot succeed. The difference is the classic case had an obvious right answer (pass `--classic`), and this one doesn't — which is why I flagged it as needing your decision rather than folding it in. The plausible options are treating an `x<N>` revision as **unreproducible** and routing it to `manual_installs_sync` (which already owns "things no package manager can reproduce", and where an install snippet could carry the actual `.snap` file), or emitting a **REPORT_ONLY** diff that names the fact without proposing a doomed command.

Detection is trivial (`revision.startswith("x")`). What's missing is the product call, and the fact that there are zero sideloaded snaps on this machine to test against.

How common: uncommon for most users, but it shows up with locally-built snaps, vendor betas shipped as files, and anything installed with `snap try`. Worth knowing whether you have any before deciding how much it matters — `snap list | awk '$3 ~ /^x/'` on both machines will tell you.

Once the flatpak fix lands I'll run the full gate and push to PR 206.

Read the issue first: `gh issue view 214`.

## The defect

`flatpak_sync` offers a target-only remote for removal with no awareness that installed refs on the target still name it as their origin; approving the removal orphans them. The install direction IS guarded (`_converge_ref` → `_remote_ready_on_target`, `src/pcswitcher/jobs/flatpak_sync.py:667` and `:716`); the remove direction has none — `_diff_flatpak_remotes` (`:328`) emits the REMOVE diff from presence alone and `_converge_remote`'s REMOVE branch (`:639`) runs `flatpak remote-delete` unconditionally.

What makes it dangerous: the dependent ref is often installed identically on BOTH machines, so it produces no diff and never appears in the review. The user approves a remote deletion whose `detail` is `None` — nothing states the consequence.

## Required approach

Follow the apt collateral pattern (D-30, `docs/adr/adr-020-declarative-package-convergence.md`), NOT the install direction's hard refusal:

- At **plan time**, for each remote REMOVE diff, determine which of the TARGET's installed refs name that remote as their origin, in that same scope. `plan()` already queries the target's refs (`query_target_items()`); reuse what is in hand rather than issuing new commands — do not add a per-remote query.
- Put those ref names in the diff's `detail` so the review states the consequence before the user approves. Follow the existing detail-string conventions in `packages/items.py` (`build_*_detail` helpers) — if a new helper belongs there, add it in that style; keep the wording terse and factual.
- Do NOT refuse the removal outright. Blanket refusal would block a legitimate cleanup where the refs are being removed in the same run. D-30's reasoning applies verbatim: the decision belongs in the review, informed, never as a mid-apply refusal.
- Scope matters: a remote is per-installation, so only refs in the SAME scope count as dependents. Do not cross user/system.
- A remote with no dependent refs keeps `detail=None` — no noise.

Consider whether refs approved for removal in the same run should be excluded from the dependent list. If you can do that cleanly from state already available at plan time, do it and note it; if it needs new plumbing, leave it and say so in your report rather than half-building it.

## Tests

## What went out

**Four defects fixed**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `3cf963be` | skip-always never honoured for apt/snap block-state items — shared `_drop_inert_diffs` applying the same D-08a holder rule as the write path. Also closed the same latent gap for apt's digest-derived repo items. |

**~75 new tests**, unit suite 1009 → 1104, plus 7 VM tests. The `mutates=` audit is now a live guard that fails on any new ungated write.

My REPORT_ONLY skip-always finding was wrong as stated — that branch is unreachable. Challenging it surfaced the real, larger defect: the checkbox UI offered two of the three promised choices for *every* item class. And my brief for the snap fix asserted that `snap refresh` preserves confinement; it preserves the **target's**, which is backwards for exactly the source-classic case, so the flag is now passed unconditionally from the source.

The matrix agent also audited my own citations and found one that didn't hold up (K2, apt target-sudo) — now a real test.

## Still open

- **#214** closes on merge.
- **Sideloaded snaps** — no issue filed yet; it needs your product call on the diff class first. Run `snap list | awk '$3 ~ /^x/'` on both machines to see whether you have any.
- **Two narrative expectations from your examples remain unimplemented**: nothing links a repo/key removal to a machine-specific package that still needs it, and there's no "last package from this source" prompt. Both are documented in the matrix (C26/N7, N6); neither is a regression.
- **The #208 D9 verdict** — whether a system-wide `refresh.hold` masks per-snap `held` notes — is what this CI run will finally answer. If it comes back false, the snap hold capture must move before the sync-window hold is applied.

def _maybe_check_for_update(console: Console, *, no_version_check: bool) -> None:
    """Best-effort startup check for a newer stable release; offer to upgrade inline.

    Non-fatal ONLY up to the point the on-disk installation is modified. Once
    `uv tool install` runs, the current process may be stale (a later lazy
    import would load a mismatched new module), so we must not keep executing:
    on a successful upgrade we re-exec the new binary, and on any failure after
    the install started we exit and tell the user how to recover. Everything
    before that boundary (check failure, offline, declined prompt, or `uv` not
    even launchable) warns and lets the current command proceed.

    Skips entirely for `--no-version-check`, `PCSWITCHER_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`, a
    help request (`--help`/`-h`), and non-interactive runs (either stdin or
    stdout not a TTY).

    Args:
        console: Rich console to print status to.
        no_version_check: If True, skip the check (from `--no-version-check`).

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: After the install has touched disk and either failed
            (recover via `self update`) or succeeded but the automatic restart
            could not happen (re-run the command). Never raised before the
            install is attempted.
    """
    # A help request would otherwise block on the upgrade prompt before the help
    # text renders; `pc-switcher <cmd> --help` should print help immediately.
    help_requested = "--help" in sys.argv or "-h" in sys.argv
    if (
        no_version_check
        or help_requested
        or os.environ.get("PCSWITCHER_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK")
        or not is_interactive(console)
    ):
        return

Confirmed — your hypothesis is right, and my earlier explanation was wrong.

**Local:** `0.5.1.post16.dev0+05d8293` — resolves against the `v0.5.1` tag, so it's *newer* than 0.5.1 and no upgrade is offered.

**CI:** `0.0.0+post.1.dev.0.63837dc` — that `0.0.0` is dunamai's "no tags found" fallback. `actions/checkout@v7` defaults to `fetch-depth: 1` and fetches no tags, so uv-dynamic-versioning has nothing to resolve against. Then `0.0.0 < 0.5.1` → "a new stable version is available" → prompt → abort.

So it doesn't fail *sometimes* — in CI it fails **always**, and would have from the moment that test was written. My "only when a newer release exists" was the right mechanism described against the wrong version number.

That raises a question my fix doesn't answer: what else in CI sees version `0.0.0`?

content.text:
Answered — and the blast radius is smaller than I feared:

**`integration-tests.yml` already uses `fetch-depth: 0`** (line 66), so tags are present and the version resolves properly there. That matters, because `install_on_target.validate` compares `target_version > source_version` and errors on a conflict — with a `0.0.0` source that comparison would misbehave on every VM run. It doesn't, because that workflow was set up correctly.

**`ci.yml` (lint + unit) uses the default shallow checkout**, so every job there sees `0.0.0+post.N.dev.0.<sha>`. The only test that read the version was the one that just broke; everything else is version-agnostic, which is why CI showed exactly one failure.

So my fix is at the right level — the test shouldn't depend on version resolution at all — but there's a latent trap: any future unit test or code path that compares versions will silently see `0.0.0` in CI and be wrong in a way that's invisible locally. Adding `fetch-depth: 0` to `ci.yml` would close that for roughly zero cost on a repo this size. It's a CI-config change outside this phase's scope, so I haven't touched it — say the word if you want it.

One unrelated thing I noticed: your local venv reports `0.5.1.post16.dev0` while HEAD is 153 commits past `v0.5.1` — the stale version stamp. `uv sync --reinstall-package pcswitcher` re-stamps it if the number ever matters to you.

Waiting on the CI run now.

Both integration failures are in **my new tests**, and both are test bugs, not product bugs. More importantly:

**#208 D9 is answered — the assumption holds.** `TestSnapHoldCaptureTiming` passed against real snapd: a system-wide `refresh.hold` does not mask per-snap `held` notes. And `TestBlockStateDecisionRoundTrip` passed, so the hold skip-always fix works end-to-end on real machines.

Now your point about the patch. You're right, and the reason other tests don't break is damning for what I did:

`tests/unit/cli/test_version_check.py` fakes a TTY in ~10 tests — and every one of them also patches `get_this_version` **and** `get_highest_release`. They never let real version resolution or a real network call happen. Mine was the only test that faked a TTY and then let the actual update check run. So the repo already had a convention and I bypassed it with an env var.

Reverting the patch and fixing the root cause:
