content.text:
You were right to push back — and the reason you were surprised turned out to be the useful part.

`tests/unit/cli/test_version_check.py` fakes a TTY in about ten tests, and every one of them also stubs `get_this_version` **and** `get_highest_release`. None of them ever lets real version resolution or a real network call happen. Mine was the only TTY-faking test that did, so it was the only one exposed. The convention already existed; I reached for an env var instead of looking.

Two separate things were wrong, and `fetch-depth: 0` only fixes one:

**`ci.yml` fetched no tags**, so lint and unit jobs built the package as `0.0.0+post.N.dev.0.<sha>` — older than every release. That's a real defect independent of any test: every CI job reported a nonsense version, and any future code or test that compares versions would have been silently wrong in CI while passing locally. `integration-tests.yml` already had `fetch-depth: 0`; `ci.yml` now matches.

**The test still reached the live GitHub API.** `fetch-depth: 0` alone would have made it pass today — correct version beats latest release — but it would break again the day a release exists that's newer than the branch's nearest tag, and it makes a network call on every run (the CI log even showed `GITHUB_TOKEN not set, using unauthenticated GitHub API (60 req/hr)`). So the test now stubs both version functions like its siblings. Both fixes are in `0ee1b009`.

One thing I got wrong along the way: I first stubbed `get_highest_release` to return `None`, which crashed with `AttributeError` — the function is typed `-> Release` and never returns `None`, so the CLI is right not to guard it. Corrected to a stub release pinned to the same version.

## Meanwhile, the integration run answered the real question

**#208 D9 holds.** `TestSnapHoldCaptureTiming` passed against real snapd: a system-wide `refresh.hold` does not mask per-snap `held` notes, so capturing inside the sync window is safe and the code comment's assumption is now verified rather than asserted. `TestBlockStateDecisionRoundTrip` also passed — the hold skip-always fix works end-to-end on real machines.

64 passed, 8 skipped, and the only 2 failures are both my own new tests with faulty premises: one assumed `apt-get update` exits non-zero on an unreachable repo (it exits 0 with a `W:` warning), the other enabled `flatpak_sync` on VMs that have no flatpak, which fails validation before any job runs. An agent is fixing both now.

"""The running package's version must be derived from a git tag, never the 0.0.0 fallback.

Deliberately not a unit test: it asserts a property of the ENVIRONMENT the package was
built in, which a unit test would have to mock away to stay hermetic. It needs no VMs
either — it lives here because `tests/integration/` is the phase whose checkout fetches
full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), which is exactly the condition under test.

`uv-dynamic-versioning` derives the version from the nearest reachable tag. A checkout
that fetches no tags leaves it nothing to resolve against, and it falls back to
`0.0.0+post.<n>.dev.0.<sha>` — a version that silently reads as OLDER than every release.
Two real behaviours break on that, neither of them noisily:

- `InstallOnTargetJob.validate` refuses to run when the target's version is newer than the
  source's; a `0.0.0` source inverts that comparison against any real target.
- The startup update check offers an upgrade to the newest release and, on a TTY, blocks
  on its prompt — which is how this was found.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess

from pcswitcher.version import Version, get_this_version

# The version dunamai produces when no tag is reachable. Compared on the release triple
# alone: the fallback's local/dev suffix carries the commit sha, which varies per run.
_NO_TAG_FALLBACK = Version.parse("0.0.0")


def test_version_resolves_from_a_tag_not_the_no_tag_fallback() -> None:
    """A tagless checkout yields 0.0.0 and silently reads as older than every release."""
    version = get_this_version()

    assert (version.major, version.minor, version.patch) != (
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.major,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.minor,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.patch,
    ), (
        f"pc-switcher resolved to {version.semver_str()}, uv-dynamic-versioning's "
        "no-tag fallback. The checkout fetched no tags — a workflow step is missing "
        "`fetch-depth: 0`. Every version comparison in this run is against a version "
        "that reads as older than every release."
    )


def test_a_tag_is_actually_reachable_from_head() -> None:
    """The cause, asserted directly: `git describe` is what the build reads.

    Separate from the assertion above so a failure says whether the tag is missing from
    the checkout or the build resolved it wrongly, rather than leaving both open.
    """
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "describe", "--tags", "--abbrev=0"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        "no tag is reachable from HEAD in this checkout, so the version cannot resolve: "
        f"{result.stderr.strip()}"
    )

"""The running package's version must be derived from a git tag, never the 0.0.0 fallback.

Deliberately not a unit test: it asserts a property of the ENVIRONMENT the package was
built in, which a unit test would have to mock away to stay hermetic. It needs no VMs
either — it lives here because `tests/integration/` is the phase whose checkout fetches
full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), which is exactly the condition under test.

`uv-dynamic-versioning` derives the version from the nearest reachable tag. A checkout
that fetches no tags leaves it nothing to resolve against, and it falls back to
`0.0.0+post.<n>.dev.0.<sha>` — a version that silently reads as OLDER than every release.
Two real behaviours break on that, neither of them noisily:

- `InstallOnTargetJob.validate` refuses to run when the target's version is newer than the
  source's; a `0.0.0` source inverts that comparison against any real target.
- The startup update check offers an upgrade to the newest release and, on a TTY, blocks
  on its prompt — which is how this was found.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess

from pcswitcher.version import Version, get_this_version

# The version dunamai produces when no tag is reachable. Compared on the release triple
# alone: the fallback's local/dev suffix carries the commit sha, which varies per run.
_NO_TAG_FALLBACK = Version.parse("0.0.0")


def test_version_resolves_from_a_tag_not_the_no_tag_fallback() -> None:
    """A tagless checkout yields 0.0.0 and silently reads as older than every release."""
    version = get_this_version()

    assert (version.major, version.minor, version.patch) != (
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.major,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.minor,
        _NO_TAG_FALLBACK.patch,
    ), (
        f"pc-switcher resolved to {version.semver_str()}, uv-dynamic-versioning's "
        "no-tag fallback. The checkout fetched no tags — a workflow step is missing "
        "`fetch-depth: 0`. Every version comparison in this run is against a version "
        "that reads as older than every release."
    )


def test_a_tag_is_actually_reachable_from_head() -> None:
    """The cause, asserted directly: `git describe` is what the build reads.

    Separate from the assertion above so a failure says whether the tag is missing from
    the checkout or the build resolved it wrongly, rather than leaving both open.
    """
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "describe", "--tags", "--abbrev=0"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        "no tag is reachable from HEAD in this checkout, so the version cannot resolve: "
        f"{result.stderr.strip()}"
    )
